description: Normalized test seed for Personalized Learning Journey API Contract v1. Source content retained; operational state initially empty.

extraction_notes: HTML source uses levels and quizzes; API calls them milestones and challenges.
Question text, choices, correct answers, explanation text, difficulty, chapter tags, and CMS row refs originate from HTML.
All IDs and version 1 values are generated deterministically for mock testing.
Source has 184 image markers but no image URLs; missing image URLs are not fabricated.

Source contains no reliable durations, challenge descriptions, per-user progress, attempts, or personalized assignments; durations/descriptions are null and a clearly labeled zero-progress demo assignment is generated for endpoint smoke tests.
Stored correct_answer and explanation fields are backend-only; omit them in ungraded API responses.
Source options are in original order; attempt start must persist a shuffled option_order, while option_key A/B/C/D is generated for delivered order.
Only SINGLE_CHOICE items are present in source: 379 questions have 4 options and 2 have 3. No True/False items are inferred.

config.attempt_creation: Server generates and freezes question/option order, correct answer snapshot and new attempt_id.

journey_templates.description: Learning journey for the Swedish B-licence theory test.

milestones.title: Your first drive: read the road
milestones.description: Learn the language of the road first: warning signs, the lines painted on the tarmac and who goes first at a junction.

milestones.title: Into town
milestones.description: Traffic lights, cyclists, one-way streets and the slow vehicles you share town roads with.

milestones.title: The parking challenge
milestones.description: Can you park here? Signs, time plates and the odd-or-even date rule that catches everyone out.

milestones.title: The open road
milestones.description: Out of town: overtaking, meeting oncoming traffic and what to do when a moose steps onto the road.

milestones.title: Motorway
milestones.description: Joining, overtaking and leaving at high speed, and how far you travel before you even react.

milestones.title: Night & winter
milestones.description: Headlights, black ice and the tiredness that creeps up on a long, dark drive.

milestones.title: Under the hood
milestones.description: Get the car ready for a trip: dashboard warning lights, tyres and everyday checks.

milestones.title: Road trip!
milestones.description: Friends in the back and a caravan behind: peer pressure, trailers, weights and whether you fit under the bridge.

milestones.title: When things go wrong
milestones.description: Breakdowns, accidents and the defensive habits that keep you out of trouble in the first place.

milestones.title: Licence day
milestones.description: The rules around your licence and how to drive greener. After this level, you are ready for the test.

questions.question_text: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Warning for slippery road conditions
Warning for curvy road
Warning for a narrow road stretch
Prohibited to drive with summer tyres all year

options.text: Alternative A
Alternative B
Alternative C
Alternative D

questions.question_text: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Warning for traffic queue
Warning for oncoming traffic
Warning for a narrow road stretch
Warning for Police held traffic control

questions.question_text: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Warning for sharp curve, direction left
Warning for left turn
Warning for side wind coming from the left
Warning for caterpillars

questions.question_text: People working at the roadside are not immortal. We should adjust speed and show consideration for them. What does this road sign mean?

options.text: End of road construction site
Warning for construction site
Warning for weak roadside
Warning for ore miners

questions.question_text: This is a road sign common at bridges. What does it mean?

options.text: Warning for strong wind coming from the left
Warning for strong wind coming from the right
I have to stay in the right lane
I have to stay in the left lane

questions.question_text: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: It means that there is heightened risk for traffic queue here, I should be extra catious of the distance to the car in front of me and be prepared to lower my speed
It means I can not overtake or change my lane here
It means one lane will cease and I have to be aware of traffic which changes the lane
It means the highway ends a bit further up on this road

questions.explanation: Traffic queues might be dangerous, and the risk of an accident increases. This sign warns you of that, so pay extra attention!

questions.question_text: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Warning for a level-crossing with railway, gates are missing
Warning for subway crossing with gates
Warning for train museum
Warning for a railway crossing with gates

questions.question_text: What does these road markings mean?

options.text: They mark the middle of the road and split oncoming lane from my lane
They mark the shoulder of the road, the tighter ones are for higher speed
They mark the oncoming traffic land and my lane, the tighter ones means it's obscured sight soon
They mark an intersection is coming up

questions.explanation: This is the most common road marking there is. It splits your road into the ones going your way and oncoming traffic. The tighter ones is tighter because the maximum speed is lower there, usually 50 km/h or less.

questions.question_text: What does these road markings mean?

options.text: It tells me soon the line might be a full drawn line so I should not overtake now
They mark the middle of the road and with these lines I can also tell that the maximum speed is 70 km/h or more
They mark the side of my lane and the other lane in the same direction
It marks the shoulder of the road

questions.explanation: They mark the middle of the road and split oncoming lane from your lane, and since they are tight and long it means soon it will be obscured view, not a good place to overtake or otherwise cross this line!

questions.question_text: What does these road markings mean?

options.text: It marks the shoulder of the road
This is a bicycle and moped class II path
These marks show the pedestrian lane
It's a lane for motorcycles

questions.explanation: The shoulder line is usually about 1:2 in length to the space in between lines, and the should is used for pedestrians, cyclists, moped class II, A-tractors and other slower vehicles. It can also be used to help others by letting others pass, if possible.

questions.question_text: What does these road markings mean?

options.text: It is a full drawn line and it is prohibited to cross over it
This means no exit allowed for lorries
This means an exit lane is coming up
Further down the road, it will turn into a motorway, I should look for an exit unless I plan to enter the motorway

questions.explanation: A fully drawn line can exist for many different reasons, but the most common reason is because it might be dangerous to cross it. So don't.

questions.question_text: What does these road markings mean?

options.text: If the fully drawn line is closest to my vehicle, it means I have a fully drawn line but the oncoming traffic does not
If the fully drawn line is furtherest from my vehicle, it means I have a fully drawn line but the oncoming traffic does not
If the fully drawn line is closest my vehicle, it means they have a fully drawn line, but i have not
Both oncoming traffic and me have a fully drawn line

questions.explanation: Usually the view is obscured for the trafficants which has the fully drawn line, but not for oncoming traffic so they may cross it if it's safe to do so.

questions.question_text: What does these road markings mean?

options.text: This area is prohibited for traffic
This is an entrance lane for entering highway
Police may need their own lane, and then it's marked like this
This is a parking area for lorries

questions.explanation: Do you see the fully drawn lines in this road marking? That means "No". So don't be here, easy to remember!

questions.question_text: What does these road markings mean?

options.text: If I have the fully drawn line on my side, that one is for me. The other one warns the oncoming traffic that the line may soon be a fully drawn line and that it's not appropriate to overtake or cross the line here

If oncoming traffic have the fully drawn line on my side, that one is for me. The other one warns me that the line may soon be a fully drawn line and that it's not appropriate to overtake or cross the line here
It means that a speed decrease is about to come further up the road
It means the road is about to get more narrow

questions.explanation: Warning line and full drawn line on the same stretch of road? Overtaking is a bad idea for both directions, but also illegal for the one who has the full line closest.

questions.question_text: What does these road markings mean?

options.text: The marking is used where it's inappropriate to cross the warning line because of traffic conditions
The marking is used where it's prohibited to cross the warning line because of traffic conditions
I may not drive here, lorries only
The marking is used where it's inappropriate to cross the full drawn lines because of traffic conditions.

questions.explanation: If you look further up the road at this situation, you are almost certainly going to see that the view is obscured for some reason. This is why they have marked the road like this, to warn you not to cross the line here.

questions.question_text: What does these road markings mean?

options.text: This is a stop line and it tells me where to stop if I have a stop sign or a red light
This is a fully drawn line and I must not cross it
No passage allowed
No entrance allowed

questions.explanation: One of the swedish traffic laws that is absolutely vital to know and obey. Should the police see you cross over a stop line at a stop sign without coming to a full stop first, or drive when the traffic light is red, not only will they give you an expensive fine but they will also take your driving licence away. No exceptions.

questions.question_text: What does these road markings mean?

options.text: This is where I stop if I have to, in a situation where I have a give way sign
This means Stop at the line before I can go
There are several lanes here, pay extra attention
Speed obstacle, so called "shark teeth" may risa up from this lane if I speed

questions.explanation: The marking indicates the line that vehicles should not cross when the driver is yielding/giving way.

questions.question_text: What does these road markings mean?

options.text: It means speed bump
It means pedestrian crosswalk
It means cyclists have priority
It means Police station exit/entrance

questions.explanation: The markings for speed obstacle can be seen from a distance in order to help you slow down your speed safely and economically by releasing the gas pedal in good time before. So check for them.

questions.question_text: What does these road markings mean?

options.text: It's a probation, you can not park here, nor can you stop here.
It's a pickup spot for taxis.
It's a cargo zone, so you may only stop here if you are to pick up or leave some kind of cargo in your car
It's an exit from a hospital

questions.explanation: It means no stopping or parking. So just proceed please.

questions.question_text: What does these road markings mean?

options.text: If I am to park here, I need a permit for that
This means only people in a wheelchair can use this parking
It means no parking, unless one can be categorized as either old people, people with a handicap that is a hindrance to them in traffic or pets with special needs, they may use this parking.
It means handicapped driver's lane

questions.explanation: It's not enough that you are in a wheelchair. You must have a permit. And for that permit, you don't need to be in a wheelchair, that is just the common symbol for the permit needed. Amputees usually get them too.

questions.question_text: What does these road markings mean?

options.text: It means this lane is for commuting traffic only
It means road vehicles with 8 passengers or more are limited to this lane
It means no cars are allowed, only buses
It means this is a bus stop

questions.explanation: It's not enough for a bus to be a bus, which is an engine driven road vehicle with more than 8 passengers in order to use this lane - this bus must also be commuting. For example, city bus, region bus, those may use this lane. Not a rented tourist bus per se, in that case an additional sign says so. Same is true for taxis, additional sign will say so if they can use it.

questions.question_text: What does these road markings mean?

options.text: It means the maximum speed is 30 m/h here
It means the recommended speed is 30 km/h here
It means 30 meters between vehicles at all times here
It means only lorries exceeding 30 tons (30 000 kilograms) may use this lane

questions.explanation: Even though a black road sign with white number is usually a recommended speed, in this case you must consider the shape of the sign. It's round, which in combination with a maximum speed makes it a probation. So this is a stronger signal for you that in this lane, it's maximum 30 km/h allowed. Not recommended, forbidden. Stay under 30 km/h.

questions.question_text: What does these road markings mean?

options.text: It's a marking that informs of the designated term of the road, in this case Europe classed road number 4, or E4
It's means this road leads to Europe highway number 4, E4.
It means this lane will soon become E4
It means I am about to enter a highway with the name E4

questions.explanation: In the cities there might be several highways joining roads. So driving on a stretch of road through Stockholm for example, you may find yourself being driving both on E4 and E20 at the same time. When they split up and go different directions, you will see this sign to know which lane to proceed in.

questions.question_text: What does this road sign mean for you as a driver if you encounter it on the road which you are currently on?

options.text: Vehicles on the oncoming road from both the right has to give way to vehicles on the road on which I am currently driving in the next junction
Warning that vehicles on this road must give way for vehicles coming from both left and right in the coming intersection
Right hand rule for all vehicles on my road
Exit rule applies for everyone in the coming junction

questions.explanation: This is true! However, if a driver from the left wishes to enter the road straight (not turning their right) they must also give way for you.

questions.question_text: You approach a junction with this road sign. What alternative is correct?

options.text: I slow down in good time to show others my intention to give way, I also check for an opportunity to proceed without disturbing others
I keep my speed and proceed, I don't have to stop unless someone else has to brake hard for me
I speed up in order to show others my intention to go first
I stop at the road sign to make sure that I am yielding to others

questions.explanation: Show others your intentions! The safest driver is the predictable driver. The give way sign means you have to give others way, if they are there for you to give way to. If no one is there, you may proceed with caution.

questions.question_text: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Yield sign or Give way sign, it means I have to give way for everyone in this situation
It means I have to stop in this intersection before proceeding
It means general warning
It means the traffic on the other road must give me the way

questions.explanation: You are allowed to continue without stopping, but only if it is safe and you do not disturb others. If the other driver has to even ease off of their gas pedal, you did not properly yield!

questions.question_text: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: It means Stop. I have to stop at the stop line and after that, it's like a give way sign, I may proceed only if it's safe to do so and I can do it with out disturbing other traffic.
It means I have to stop at the stop sign and then give way for others as I continue to drive.
It means all motor driven vehicles have to stop before proceeding
It means I stop if there is other traffic on the road

questions.explanation: You stop at the stop line, not the traffic road sign itself. If there is no line visible due to snow or worn out road markings, you stop just before your vehicle enters the other road. Make sure you see them, make sure they see you!

questions.question_text: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: This sign means major road or main road. All streets attaching to this road will have either a stop sign or a give way sign, so others are to give me the way.
This sign means I am driving on a rural road, snow and leaves and dust removing will be handled by the city authorities.
This road sign means right hand rule applies.
I must give way to others after this sign

questions.explanation: Major road has a lot of rules, but the most important one is others are to give way for you. You may not park here, unless there are parking lots especially.

questions.question_text: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Major road ends
Crossing roads have to give way after this sign
Major road begins
No more maintenance of road after this sign

questions.explanation: Most places where it's unclear that the major road ends, this sign is put there to inform about it. If the major road continues and it's not unclear what applies, this sign might not appear. If you see it, be prepared for right handrule from here on.

questions.question_text: Which of these signs has the outcome that you must give way to vehicles from the right?

options.text: C
B
A and B
All of them

questions.explanation: Learn the signs. And never expect everyone to always follow them. Isaac Newton and the laws of physics always triumphs the rules of traffic! It is a poor comfort that you had the right of way if you're sitting in a hospital bed and cannot move your toes.

questions.question_text: Which rules apply in all junctions after this sign?

options.text: Right hand rule for junctions, and exit rule if it's from parking lots, coming from terrain, coming for property, gas station or similar
Major road, all vehicles from roads that cross this road has to give way or stop
Mutual agreement and cooperation, but no one has to give way
The center rule

questions.explanation: Major road ends, so you have to be aware if it's an exit or a junction of two or more different roads

questions.question_text: You come to this road sign combination. How do you proceed?

options.text: I adjust my speed and prepare to stop completely before the coming junction
I proceed with caution as I have to give way in 200 meters
I am extra vigilant as there will come a junction in 200 meters where others should give way for me, but not everyone follows the rules
The coming 200 meters, I have to give way in every junction

questions.explanation: The give way sign means I should give way, true. The additional sign however also tells me I also have to stop the vehicle completely before proceeding, and as I proceed after stopping at the stop line, I must give way for other traffic.

questions.question_text: You are driving in a rural area and you approach this road sign. In the junction just after, a car drives out from your right, quite close, and you hit the brakes and almost collide. What went wrong here?

options.text: After this road sign, it's no longer a major road, so right hand rule applies. I should have seen the car and been prepared to brake sooner. Also, the other driver should have been more cautious, in order to avoid an accident according to the basic law of traffic.
The other driver should have given way since it's major road.
We both should have mutually considered the other according to the basic law of traffic, since it's no longer a major road.
I must give way from both left and right since it's no longer a major road. I should have known this and have been better prepared for the situation.

questions.explanation: After the major road ends and this sign is put up, it's right hand rule. That is still a poor consolation after a collision and the other drivers neck as well as yours will hurt just as much, no matter who had the right of way.

questions.question_text: In this situation, you wish to turn left. What rules apply?

options.text: Vehicles from the right should give way for me so I should just be able to proceed, I do however drive defensive as always, prepared for misunderstanding
Right hand rule applies in this situation, it doesn't matter that the road is smaller
I cannot turn left here, only bus and lorry can go left due to the bus rule
The road is going to become wider after the junction

questions.question_text: Which rule is applicable in this situation?

options.text: Right hand rule
Exit rule
Give way rule
Stop rule

questions.question_text: The bus from the right hesitates. Should you drive even though it's right hand rule?

options.text: I cooperate with the bus driver since a bus might need extra space to turn, so I proceed yet with caution.
No, since it's right hand rule and I must yield for the bus if it comes from the right
Right hand rule does not apply to buses and long haulers
I have to wait until the bus has turned before I decide in order to see behind it

questions.explanation: This is a tricky one, because by law, you should wait. By reality however, the bus might not be able to go before you have moved out of the way.

questions.question_text: What is correct in this situation (multiple stop)

options.text: Everyone must stop at the stop line, and whoever stops first should also drive first
I stop and wait for all other cars to drive before I proceed
I stop and I also give way for cars from the right
I only have to stop if someone else is in the junction

questions.explanation: If you are the one who has stopped first, everyone else must first stop before they are allowed to go. So it makes sense that you go first.

questions.question_text: A vehicle is approacing the junction from your right. Who yields?

options.text: I yield, due to the right hand rule
He/She yields, due to my road being bigger
He/She yields, due to the exit rule
I yield, due to the exit rule

questions.explanation: You might wish to revisit the right hand rule again. If two vehicles approach each other and their courses will collide, the one coming from the right should be given the road.

questions.question_text: The car from your left is coming from a gas station. Who should give way in this situation?

options.text: The driver coming from the gas station since the exit rule applies
I should give way, since right hand rule applies
I should give way due to the exit rule
The responsibility is mutual and we should cooperate since there are no rules for this situation

questions.explanation: Gas station, so Exit rule applies. The exit rule is for exits, such as from property, gas stations, parking lots, etc.

questions.question_text: What is true in this situation if you are about to turn to the right?

options.text: If you have a green arrow, this triumphs the red light in your direction and you should proceed
I have to wait for the red light to change and then I may proceed
I may proceed but I have to give way due to the give way sign
I cannot turn to the right in this situation

questions.explanation: Here is the order of authority: Follow first and foremost a police officers instructions. If there are no police (which is typically the case) you follow traffic lights if you have those. If not, you reside to traffic road signs and finally, if there are none of the above, the give way rules of right hand rule, exit rule, etc.

questions.question_text: What is "the blocking rule" and what does it mean?

options.text: The blocking rule is an easy way to remember the different laws and regulations that prohibit us as trafficants to hinder each other unneccessarily in different intersections, pedestrian crosswalks, intersections, etc. Don't be unneccessarily in the way of others!
The blocking rule means I should not allow others to overtake if they will put themselves in harms way due to oncoming traffic or similar situation
It means I always drive a little faster than the speed limit so I don't block others
It means I should always keep one city block in between me and a bus, to provide space for them to maneuever.

questions.explanation: Blocking rule in mostly important in junctions and the close perimeter of junctions. What it means is basically never to drive up into something where you risk of being in the way, unless you can see that you may proceed safely.

questions.question_text: What is "the turning rule" and what does it mean?

options.text: Whenever I'm turning left, I pass through oncoming traffic lane/lanes, and I must give them way and find a gap when I can safely pass and proceed
It is prohibited to turn when I have the turning rule sign
Turning rule means the one who turns should be given the way, so that there are less vehicles in the intersection and traffic flow is smoother
Turning rule is a misunderstanding and an urban myth - It's really "Exit rule"

questions.explanation: Turning rule can basically be seen as a version of right hand rule. When you turn and pass into oncoming traffic and their lane or lanes, they come from your right. So you give them the way.

questions.question_text: How do we know who should drive first in this situation?

options.text: The oncoming traffic should drive first, since the obstacle is in my lane, so I give way
I should drive first, since the road construction is in my lane
I have to wait until the construction truck moves farther to the right side
The oncoming traffic has to use the shoulder of the road in this situation in order for me to not have to consider them

questions.explanation: The driver who encounters an obstacle in their lane has to give way. When you go home and pass this situation from the other way, the oncoming traffic will have the obstacle on their side and then they are obliged to give you the way.

questions.question_text: Regarding this image - which one of these statements is false?

options.text: I must give way to vehicles exiting from a parking lot
This car is turning left
I have to give way to this car before I can proceed due to the exit rule
Always use blinkers when turning to show your intentions to others

questions.explanation: It's a lowered pavement, so assume it is exit rule that applies to this situation.

questions.question_text: You have arrived first of 4 different cars to this road sign. What are the rules in this situation?

options.text: The one who arrives to the stop line first should also proceed first
We must all stop and then cooperate
We all have to stop and the it's right hand rule
We all have to first stop, and then apply to the exit rule

questions.explanation: Multi STOP sign means that whomever arrives first should also drive first. The others have to first stop at their stop line, so it would be inconvenient otherwise.

questions.question_text: You are at a level crossing with a railway. What is the correct statement in this situation?

options.text: I must wait until the gates are completely up and the light returns from fast blinking red to a slow white blinking light
I can drive as soon as the gates are open but must still stop before I enter the tracks
I have to wait until the light turns green
This sign tells us that there are no active railway gates, so I may drive but I must check for oncoming trains before crossing

questions.question_text: The traffic light shows green, but a police officer is standing in the middle of the intersection and holds the hand like this. What should you do?

options.text: I should abide by the police gesture and stop my vehicle until further instruction
I should slowly proceed up to the police officer and lower my window to get further instructions
I have a green light, so I should pass her by and wave back
I lower my window and pass her by and give her a high five!

questions.explanation: A police officer giving you a sign like this is always to be obeyed. Police triumphs traffic lights, traffic signs and traffic rules. Do as they say or show to you.

questions.question_text: You are going to make a turn to the right here and you have 2 cyclists behind you to your right. How do you place yourself?

options.text: I place the car slightly to the right to show my intentions and to prevent cyclists from trying to squeeze in to my right
I place myself slightly to the left to allow cyclists to pass by first
I place myself in the middle
I place the car slightly on the curb

questions.explanation: Slightly to the right to show which way I'm going and also blinkers, of course!

questions.question_text: You have stopped behind the vehicle in front of you, who has stopped for a stop sign at the stop line. Since you have come to a full stop, are you allowed to drive once the car in front of you drives off?

options.text: No, I have to come to a full stop first at the stop line or immediately before I enter the road
Yes, since I've stopped completely already I can proceed if there is no risk
Yes, but I first have to make sure that no other vehicle is affected by me
That depends on the situation, I can drive if there is no one else there

questions.explanation: Stop lines are absolute. Always stop. Always look.

questions.question_text: The traffic light shows you green, but there is also a stop sign. What is correct in this situation?

options.text: No, since I have green I can proceed but I still scan for risks before proceeding
I may proceed but I first have to stop at the stop line
The stop sign triumph the traffic light, so I have to come to a full stop and give way for cars coming from the right

questions.explanation: Traffic lights triumphs road signs. The road sign is there in case the lights are off

questions.question_text: You are approaching an intersection with a stop sign but due to snow on the road, you cannot see any stop line. Where should you stop with your vehicle?

options.text: I stop immediately before my car sticks the front out into the crossing road
At the stop sign
About 2 meters/2.2 yards before the intersection
I can choose freely since there is no visible line

questions.explanation: You have to make sure that you see as good as you can, but also that others see you as much as possible. So drive all the way up to the junction!

questions.question_text: If the traffic light signal is blinking white at a railway crossing, are you obliged to stop before crossing over?

options.text: You may cross but only if you have made sure no train is approaching
No, never.
Yes, you must always stop before crossing a railroad
Only if the gates are closing

questions.explanation: The white light tells us that no sensor detects a train nearby. However, trust your eyes. Sensors may be broken but trains are big. You will see them. So look before crossing.

questions.question_text: You come to a traffic light that just turns yellow as you pass. What is correct?

options.text: I should stop if I can do so safely, otherwise I continue to drive through the intersection
I am always allowed to drive through yellow traffic lights
Yellow is the same as red by the law, so I always have to stop
That depends on if there is a stop sign

questions.explanation: Yellow means "soon red" and you are obliged to stop if you can do it safely. If you however already passed and have to stop in the junction, proceed instead.

questions.question_text: You are driving towards an intersection and the traffic light turns green. A school class of small children with reflex vests starts to cross, led by a teacher. What should you do?

options.text: I stop and wait for the children to pass, I am not allowed to separate the children from their supervisor
I have a green light, I go
I allow the first half of the children to go, then it's my turn
I seek eye contact with the teacher, mutual responsibility in this situation

questions.explanation: Children are to be shown extra consideration in traffic. Sometimes teachers make mistkes. You are not allowed to put children at risk just because of that, so you wait until they have all passed safely.

questions.question_text: What does this light mean?

options.text: Stop, do not pass. Train is coming on the railway.
Train is coming but as long as the gates are not down, you should drive in order to not be a disturbance to others
Train has passed and you may go.
Fire fighter train is alarmed, keep a lookout for the heroes!

questions.explanation: Do not under any circumstances be close to the railway when this light shows. Trains takes several kilometers of braking distance to stop in case they come full speed. Drive through the gates if you have to. Just leave the car on the tracks if you have to! Get out of there!

questions.question_text: Where should you stop in this situation?

options.text: I stop on the other side of the railway, behond the other car at the red traffic light
I stop just before the gate at the railway crossing.
I stop at the railway since the gates are not closed
I change the lane and stop to the left of the car at the traffic light, since both lanes continue in my direction

questions.question_text: Whom should give way for whom?

options.text: A cyclist should give way for a car if the cyclist choose to ride the bicycle on a pedestrian crossing
A car should give way for a bus leaving the bus stop if the road has a maximum speed limit of 70 km/h
A cyclist should always give way for a car on a cyclist passage
A bus should give way for a car when the bus leaves the bus stop if the road has a maximum speed limit of 50 km/h

questions.explanation: A cyclist is allowed to ride the bike over a pedestrian crosswalk but have to give way to all other trafficants in that case.

questions.question_text: Which way must you go in the roundabout in order to get to E4 motorway?

options.text: I must take the second exit and proceed straight in the roundabout
I must take the first exit and turn right in the roundabout
I must take the third exit and turn left in the roundabout
I have to perform a U-turn in the roundabout and take the fourth exit

questions.explanation: Green road sign means motorway, and the arrow points straight, so second exit and proceed.

questions.question_text: In which order should you do what things before making a turn in a junction?

options.text: I check my surroundings with the mirrors and then use my blinkers, then I slowdown if needed and check the blindspot before I turn the wheel to make sure nobody is there either, then turn and proceed
I slow down, use the blinkers, check my blind spot and turn
I check my blind spot and then the mirrors, slow down and use blinkers just before I turn
I give gas and pull the parking brake, steering wheel slightly to my direction, prepared to counter if I drift too much

questions.explanation: First make sure you know what you have around you. Then warn others that something is about to happen. Decrease speed. Check again making sure it's okay to go and then proceed.

questions.question_text: A person is pointing her stick out like this at a pedestrian crossing. What does this mean?

options.text: It means that she is vision impaired and signals with the angle of her stick that she intends to cross the road
It means she is blind and is waiting for the noise to weaken so that she may cross safely
It means SOS, this woman requires immediate medical assistance
It's just some student gag, pay it no mind but proceed with caution

questions.explanation: Vision impaired persons are depending on all drivers to see them and understand their signs. A stick held straight up-down means they will wait, but if they point it diagonally like this, they are about to start walking.

questions.question_text: What does these road signs mean?

options.text: Pedestrian crossing, same meaning both signs. I have to give way for pedestrians who show intention to cross
Pedestrian crossing, I am obliged to give way for pedestrians and cyclists who show intention to cross over
Pedestrian crossing, pedestrians and cyclists are obliged to give me the way but I must be careful anyway
I give way for pedestrians here, but only if there is also a speed bump in close proximity to the pedestrian crossing

questions.explanation: You must allow pedestrians to cross the street, but cyclists are supposed to give way for you. Cyclists however are the shapeshifters of traffic, since they can step off their bicycle and lead it, thus becoming pedestrians in a flash!

questions.question_text: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Narrow passage of road, I must give way for oncoming traffic
Narrow passage, oncoming traffic give way for me
Prohibited to pass oncoming traffic on the right side
Prohibited to drive from this direction

questions.explanation: Give way for oncoming traffic. You wait, they go. Once you have a window of opportunity, you may go.

questions.question_text: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Oncoming traffic gives way, I drive first but I am as always prepared to yield if they don't
Oncoming traffic should be given way
Prohibited to pass vehicles on the right side
I cannot drive this way, I must re-route and come another road

questions.explanation: This road sign means that the oncoming traffic is supposed to give way for you.

questions.question_text: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Cyclist parallel crossing, I should give way for cyclists and pedestrians
Warning for cyclists in this area
Cyclists have to use the cyclist lane here
Cyclist path, they are obliged to give way for cars, but I must be prepared if they do not

questions.explanation: Cycle track crossing, parallel crossing, tiger crossing, there are many names for this situation but the main thing to remember is that here, cyclists are to be given way also. Pedestrians and cyclists, yield for them.

questions.question_text: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Zip merge, we cooperate in both the lanes and the lanes become one lane soon
Zip merge, cars in the left lane go first, then the right lane
This road will be more narrow and no oncoming traffic, traffic only comes from this direction now
Warning for dangerous junction

questions.explanation: Zip merge means you adapt to the situation, no one has the right here so keep margins and try to help others in. Don't be a jerk! Drive as you'd want others to drive.

questions.question_text: What is the colour of a road sign meant to divert traffic away from a closed off road or street?

options.text: Orange
Yellow with a red board
Blue with white letters
Green with white board

questions.explanation: The sign is an orange arrow that looks quite similar in shape to those suppository pills that you insert... "downstairs". Follow the signs that divert the traffic, and you'll be back on route soon enough.

questions.question_text: Bus stops: How many meters before and after are you allowed to park?

options.text: 20 meters before and 5 meters after
10 meters before and 10 meters after
30 meters before and 30 meters after
24 meters before and 10 meters after

questions.explanation: You must allow for the bus to slow down and stop safely, and you must allow the bus some wiggle room when it leaves the stop since they are quite big. 20 meters minimum before and 5 meters minimum after.

questions.question_text: According to the law - which trafficants must be shown extra consideration?

options.text: Children, elderly and people with a handicap that is a hindrance for them in traffic
Children, bus drivers and ambulances
Children, cyclists and mopedists
Children, police cars and lorry drivers

questions.explanation: An ambulance, police or firefighter lorry might need you to clear a path and show you this by flashing blue lights, but not always. The law clearly states however that children, elderly, school patrols and trafficants with a handicap that is a hindrance for them in traffic must be shown extra consideration.

questions.question_text: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: In the coming intersection, left turn is prohibited
In the coming roundabout, third exit is prohibited
Left turns are not allowed other than for buses
I can turn left here but it's not recommended.

questions.explanation: Pretty self-explanatory sign. Do not turn left here!

questions.question_text: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: U-turn is prohibited in this intersection
U-turns are allowed only when you have a green light
U-turn is allowed only if the green light is green and it's an arrow
U-turn is mandatory here

questions.explanation: No U-turns. You have to find another way to turn around further down this road.

questions.question_text: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Customs, I have to stop at the line and follow instructions from the personel
It means I am required to pay road tax at this station
It means I may proceed but should watch out for "tull", which is an old word for moose calves
This sign is for locals only, it's the name of the city

questions.explanation: Don't disobey the custom officers. It's expensive and tiresome. Just stop at the stop line, do what they say, when they say it and you'll be out of there in no time.

questions.question_text: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: I have to stop at the stop line
I have to stop between the line and the traffic lights
I must only follow this sign if the lights are not functioning, otherwise I go up to the red traffic light and wait for green there
This is a sign for trains, not for road traffic

questions.explanation: The reason for this sign is usually that they have put the stop line slightly back, in order to create more space for buses making a turn. So don't drive up to the traffic light! Stop at the line if you have a red light.

questions.question_text: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: All vehicles must turn left here
It is forbidden to turn left here
All cars, buses and lorries have to turn left here but others may proceed to the right or straight
It's mandatory to park at this side of the street

questions.explanation: A mandatory sign like this goes for all vehicles, cyclists included. You must turn left. This sign can be used for different situations but the meaning is - you have to go this way. Mandatory direction!

questions.question_text: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: I must continue on this side of the sign, I may not pass the sign on the left
I have to turn and go back from where I came
I must not drive to the right of this sign
This is a sign for buses, not cars

questions.explanation: This sign can also be of an arrow downwards to the left instead of right, but it's more uncommon. What it means is - Drive here! Mandatory lane!

questions.question_text: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Roundabout/circulation
This means I come to a garbage center, I can leave batteries, toxic waste and other things here
The sign means I can proceed and others have to give way for me in the boutaround
I will get stuck in an endless loop if I proceed

questions.explanation: Basic rules of any swedish roundabout: You give way to everyone in every lane who is already in the roundabout, you always go counter-clockwise, and you always use blinkers to the right when you exit the roundabout. Everything else is details but these three are always there.

questions.question_text: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: This lane is for buses in commute traffic
This means buses has to drive here, they are not allowed to change lane
This is a prohibition for buses longer than 12 meters
Bus stops are in this lane only

questions.explanation: Only for buses and only if it's a bus in commute traffic (not a tourist bus), and usually there is also an additional sign that states taxi is also allowed but car drivers are not allowed otherwise, unless it's neccessary to gain access to a certain area like a store to deliver to, or similar.

questions.question_text: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Bus lane ends
No buses allowed
Bus longer than 12 meters is prohibited
Bus is not allwed to stop unless it's a tourist bus

questions.explanation: This is where the bus lane ends. A bus lane is only for buses and only if it's a bus in commute traffic (not a tourist bus), and usually there is also an additional sign that states taxi is also allowed but car drivers are not allowed otherwise, unless it's neccessary to gain access to a certain area like a store to deliver to, or similar.

questions.question_text: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Mandatory direction for all vehicles that holds dangerous goods
Lorries and buses must turn to the left
All vehicles with a trailer must turn to the left
All cars must stay away from the left road

questions.explanation: Usually, this sign is visable close to certain tunnels. When a lorry brings enough dangerous goods, certain international rules come into action due to safety and thus, we don't want them in tunnels. What if it explodes and toxic fire spreads in a tunnel full of other vehicles? So they have to choose another road, and this sign is for that.

questions.question_text: You discover that you have forgotten your cell phone at home on the kitchen table. Typical! Just after, you see this sign in an intersection. What do you do?

options.text: I turn around by entering left or right, depending on the situation, and then find a good place to turn around there instead. No U-turn allowed here.
I make a threepoint turn, since U-turn is forbidden here.
I drive as if I'm going to turn left, then I turn left again at the intersection. That's not a U-turn!
I keep driving, since turning is prohibited here.

questions.explanation: Turning is allowed, just go around the block or take a street to either side and find a good place! U-turn is prohibited in this specific intersection, nothing else is said.

questions.question_text: You drive in the left of two lanes going your way and you see this sign. Further up is the same sign but with no red diagonal line. What must you be aware of here?

options.text: A junction or exit is probably coming up, I must be alert
This means no buses allowed, so I must be ready if a bus changes lane
This just means the bus lane ends, I drive a car so it's of no interest to me
It means buses may come from the opposite direction, I must give way

questions.explanation: Most times when this road sign is coming, it means there is a junction and the bus lane might continue soon. Be prepared for traffic from the right!

questions.question_text: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Mandatory cyclist lane. Moped class II may also drive here, unless stated otherwise on an additional sign
Bicyclists, pedestrians and mopeds may drive here
Cyclists can choose if they want to cycle here or if they want to go as fast as cars, then they may cycle on the ordinary road in the car lanes
Prohibited to cycle here

questions.explanation: At a mandatory sign, normally all other kinds of traffic is prohibited. Here, only cyclists and moped class II may travel, nothing else!

questions.question_text: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Pedestrian path. No vehicles allowed other than for crossing the path.
School proximity, drive careful
Forbidden for children to walk without an adult here
Children playing, be advised!

questions.explanation: At a mandatory sign, normally all other kinds of traffic is prohibited. Here, only pedestrians are allowed. You may slowly and carfully cross over if the situation allows it but nothing else!

questions.question_text: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Pedestrian and cyclist common path. Moped class II can drive here unless stated otherwise on an additional sign
Fossile fuel-free area. Only electric vehicles allowed
No bicyclists or pedestrians allowed
All trafficants must give way for cars in this path

questions.explanation: At a mandatory sign, normally all other kinds of traffic is prohibited. Here, only pedestrians, cyclists, and moped class II are allowed.

questions.question_text: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Here there is 2 different paths, one for pedestrians and one other for cyclists and moped class II
Here there is 2 different paths, one for pedestrians and one other for cyclists and moped class I
A shared path for everyone
On this bus, you may bring your bicycle

questions.explanation: At a mandatory sign, normally all other kinds of traffic is prohibited. Here, only cyclists and pedestrians are allowed, but they also have different paths

questions.question_text: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Riders on horse has to ride on this path, they may not use the road next to it (pedestrians can be here too but no one else)
Riders can be here and mopeds, cyclists and pedestrians, but cars and motorcycles including dirtbikes, is prohibited
Warning for riders on horses, proceed with care in order to not freighten the animal
Mandatory to climb off of your horse and lead it on this path

questions.explanation: At a mandatory sign, normally all other kinds of traffic is prohibited. Here, only riders and their horse and pedestrians are allowed. No cyclists or anything else!

questions.question_text: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Mandatory path for snowmobiles
Warning for snowmobiles
Prohibited to drive a snowmobile, a four-wheel terrain vehicle, a sleigh or similar vehicle
Raindeer mating area. Proceed slowly so that your dsnowmobile does not disturb the animals

questions.explanation: At a mandatory sign, normally all other kinds of traffic is prohibited. Here, only snowmobiles and pedestrians are allowed (yes, you may also ski here).

questions.question_text: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: One way street (to the right)
I have to turn right here
I must not turn right here
Cyclists may turn left here but not me

questions.explanation: One way street, usually put up at the entrance of the street. No oncoming traffic should occur, but you never know, be careful.

questions.question_text: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Dead end street. You will not be able to continue here, you must turn around on this street.
T stands for "Tunnelbana" and it means Subway in swedish
This road is prohibited to use unless you have clearance to go here by swedish Transport Agency or Police
This is a parallel street to the major road

questions.explanation: Dead end, sometimes at these roads you will have a place to turn around and sometimes not. Make sure you know what to do if you drive further.

questions.question_text: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Bus stop
Bus lane
Bus parking
Buses must not be overtaken

questions.explanation: This sign is usually put up at school bus stops as well, with an additional sign stating during which hours.

questions.question_text: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Speed camera
Police surveillance cameras in this area
Road tax cameras on this road
No cameras allowed beyond this point

questions.explanation: This should not be important for you, since you always follow the speed limit. Just in case you missed a dspeed sign, there will be one just before this sign, which means you have a speed camera coming up.

questions.question_text: What is the correct description of this sign?

options.text: This is a cyclist street. Car can only drive maximum 30 km/h and must park in designated parking lots, also give way for every cyclist and others in this street
This is a cyclist street. Car can only drive maximum 20 km/h and must park in designated parking lots, cyclists give way for cars in this street
This is a cyclist street. Car can only drive maximum 45 km/h and must park in designated parking lots, also cyclists and mopeds give way to cars in this street
This is a cyclist street. Car can only drive maximum 5 km/h and parking is prohibited, also right hand rule for everyone except moped class II

questions.explanation: You must adapt the speed to cyclists in this area.

questions.question_text: Your are passing this road sign with your car. What rules apply here?

options.text: I must proceed in walking speed (5-7 km/h but no faster than 7 km/h) and I give way to pedestrians
I must proceed slowly, maximum 7-10 km/h, pedestrians give way for me
I may not drive a car here
This sign means I can go no faster than 20 km/h and give way for pedestrians and cyclists

questions.explanation: In a home zone, you proceed at the same speed as the average pedestrian. You must also give them the way. When you leave the area, exit rule applies.

questions.question_text: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: It means I cannot enter this road this way with any vehicle
It means only vehicles with 2 wheels may enter this way
It means I have to proceed at walking speed
It means all traffic prohibited, pedestrians included

questions.explanation: This is sometimes confused with one way street, since it's put up at one way streets end. But one way street sign looks like this:

questions.question_text: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: It means all vehicle traffic is prohibited, pedestrians may proceed
It means No motor vehicles allowed except for electric bicycles and electric kickbikes
It means parking is limited to designated parking spots in this area
It means one way street

questions.explanation: This is an easy one, because it holds no information other than the fact that since it's a circular sign with a red board and a yellow background but no further information, it just means "No". So no vehicle is allowed whatsoever, ever.

questions.question_text: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: It means all motor driven vehicles except moped class II is prohibited
It means prohibited to proceed for all cars and motorcycles
It means prohibited to drive a fossile fueled vehicle from this point
It means motorcycles to the left, cars to the right

questions.explanation: You may use a skateboard, a bicycle or any other vehicle that is not driven by an engine. Moped class II is the exception this is also okay.

questions.question_text: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: It means it is prohibited to proceed if I drive a vehicle with more than 2 wheels driven by an engine
It means no car traffic allowed
It means only electric cars from here on
It means I have entered an environment zone EURO 6, so no cars allowed

questions.explanation: This sign is generally put up where the passage is narrow, so any vehicle with more than 2 wheels cannot meet safely. Motorcycles are still okay to drive here though.

questions.question_text: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Prohibited to proceed after this sign driving a motorcycle or a moped class I
Motorcycle traffic is prohibited but all bicycles or mopeds can pass
No bikers in our town!
It means I can only pass this sign with my moped class I, no moped class II is allowed

questions.explanation: This one means both motorcycles of any kind but also mopeds class I.

questions.question_text: You arrive at this road sign and the street is narrow. What is correct?

options.text: It means it is prohibited to proceed if I drive a vehicle with more than 2 wheels driven by an engine
It means no vehicles allowed
It means no vehicles wider than 2600 mm allowed
It means only lorries from this point is allowed

questions.explanation: The narrow street combined with the normal width of a 4 wheel vehicle is the main reason for this sign to appear.

questions.question_text: You are approaching a road with this sign. What does it mean for you as the driver of a car?

options.text: All vehicle traffic is prohibited on the road in both directions, so I must choose a different route
Entry is prohibited from this direction, but the road is open to oncoming traffic.
Only motor vehicles are prohibited, but heavy vehicles in commercial transport are permitted to drive here.
The sign serves as a warning that the road is a dead end.

questions.explanation: No vehicle traffic allowed from any direction. This sign says "No", plain and simple. You may continue as a pedestrian though.

questions.question_text: You are driving your car in the city streets and you wish to proceed straight in a junction, but this sign is set up on the road from the right. What is correct?

options.text: I must be prepared that other vehicles may come from the road to the right
I may proceed straight because vehicle traffic is prohibited in the road to the right, which does not affect me
I have to turn right at this sign, since I will otherwise come to a dead end
I may not proceed straight here

questions.explanation: The road sign to the right means no entry from this end for vehicles. However, cars, bicycles and others may still come from this street and cross my path or join it. Since it might be right hand rule or obscured view, I must still be risk aware here as I proceed.

questions.question_text: You are driving your car in the city streets and you wish to proceed straight in a junction, but this sign is set up on the road going straight. What is correct?

options.text: I may not proceed, I must choose a different route
It means no pedestrians allowed beyond this point, I proceed
I have to slow down to be prepared for anything since this road sign means "other danger/hazard"
I may proceed, but I will come to a dead end

questions.explanation: The road sign means no vehicle traffic allowed. I must find another way to my destination, or park the car at a parking place and walk from here.

questions.question_text: You are riding your electric moped class II to the city today instead of your fossile fueled car, since you are environmentally conscious. This sign appears on the street. What is correct?

options.text: I may proceed
No engine vehicle allowed here, 4 wheels or 2 wheels, so I must find another route
I may only proceed if I lead my moped, since I'm considered a pedestrian if I do
I can drive any moped, bicycle or similar here, but no car, motorcycle or lorry

questions.explanation: This road sign means no vehicle traffic with motor driven vehicles, except moped class II. Since that is what you're riding, you may proceed!

questions.question_text: Which other vehicle can this vehicle be mistaken for, especially from a distance and during dark hours?

options.text: A moped since they look very alike, but the difference of speed and acceleration is huge
A bicycle, since during darkness they front light looks exactly the same
A drone, since the rear lights has the same shape and colour
A car, since this motorcycle is so big and powerful

questions.explanation: A moped and a motorcycle can often be confused since they have similar lights and size from a distance in darkness.

questions.question_text: Are you allowed to drive slower than the maximum speed limit?

options.text: Yes, if the situation requires it.
No, I must never hinder others behind me - a trafficant may never hinder or disturb other trafficants, basic traffic rule
Yes, slower is always safer, there is no law that states I have to keep the maximum speed limit of the road
No, because I don't want to be late

questions.explanation: Think of it this way - if there is a traffic queue going 20 km/h on a 90 km/h road, and you have cars in front of you: Can you go 90 km/h? What would happen? You'd crash!

questions.question_text: Why do we have speed limits?

options.text: To ensure traffic safety. The faster a vehicle travels, the longer distance is needed to come to a full stop in case of a possible collision. Some situations requires lower speed because there isn't enough room to stop.
Because the faster we drive, the more fuel we use and it affects the environment in a bad way
Because the police needs to be able to catch up to us if we misbehave
Because otherwise it would be too much fun to drive, traffic has to be boring!

questions.explanation: Speed kills. Drive safe.

questions.question_text: Slow-moving vehicles need a triangular sign in the rear. What is the maximum speed allowed for an A-tractor?

options.text: 30 km/h
40 km/h
45 km/h
50 km/h

questions.explanation: There is talk about changing it but for now, it's still 30 km/h

questions.question_text: Mopeds and motorcycles can easily be confused by even experienced drivers. True or false?

options.text: True, especially from a distance these two look the same
False. A moped is much smaller and slower than a motorcycle so it's quite easy to separate them even in the mirror
False, the moped doesn't need a registration plate and the driver doesn't need a helmet
True, but only in night when it's dark out

questions.explanation: From a distance and especially in darkness, these two types of vehicles are easily confused even by experienced drivers.

questions.question_text: Is a moped class 2 allowed to drive on this path to centrum?

options.text: Yes
No, only vehicles allowed are moped class 1 and bicycles
No, only bicycles are allowed
All mopeds and bicycles are allowed, but not motorcycles

questions.explanation: Moped class 1 is the fast moped class, allowed to go 45 km/h. Moped class 2 is only allowed to go 25 km/h, which is more in accordance with a general cycling speed.

questions.question_text: What is the maximum allowed speed for a class 1 motorised equipment vehicle?

options.text: 50 km/h
20 km/h
40 km/h
30 km/h

questions.explanation: This may be difficult to remember how to separate them, but it's just like with the mopeds - class I is number one, because they are faster, 50 km/h (moped class I is 45 km/h). Number one is the winner of any race. Class II is number two at 30 km/h (moped class II 25 km/h) and therefore didn't win the race.

questions.question_text: At which age are you allowed to drive an A-tractor if you have a B-licence?

options.text: 18 years old, since that is when I may first take the B-licence, in which AM is included
16 years old, if I have been driving for 2 years without incident
20 years old, but I may only tow a 750 kg trailer behind it
15 years old if I already have a moped class II permit

questions.explanation: A-tractor, or as it's also called EPA-tractor was originally a swedish way to allow for the youth at the farm to be able to help. Today it's more of a subculture for young people. If you have a B-licence you are automatically allowed to drive these as well.

questions.question_text: How should you read this sign if placed on the rear of a car?

options.text: This sign is put in the rear of a Slow-Moving-Vehicle, which in Swedish is shortened to LGF.
This means the vehicle is a competition vehicle, I must be alert if they accelerate
This means Police, covert operation.
It's a bumper sticker that means learner driver

questions.explanation: LGF or Slow moving vehicles can vary in their speed, usually from 30-45 km/h.

questions.question_text: What is the maximum allowed speed for motorised equipment, class 1?

options.text: 50 km/h
30 km/h
40 km/h
70 km/h

questions.explanation: motorised equipment class 1 means that the vehicle is constructed for speeds higher than 30 km/h, but the maximum speed allowed is 50 km/h.

questions.question_text: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: It means parking is not allowed here
It means stopping and parking is not allowed here
It means stopping is not allowed here
It means probation to use vehicles beyond this point

questions.explanation: You may stop to pick up passengers or drop someone off, you may load cargo into the vehicle or unload your vehicle, but as soon as any of these activities ends, you have parked. Which this sign says you can't.

questions.question_text: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: It means neither parking nor stopping is allowed here, I have to keep driving
It means no parking allowed but I may stop to pick someone up
It means no vehicles allowed beyond this point
This sign means no vehicles constructed for a speed of more than 25 km/h may proceed

questions.explanation: Probation from stopping or parking. One diagonal line means parking, an "X" means the two lines are for both stopping and parking. This is how to remember which one is which.

questions.question_text: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Parking allowed Monday-Friday maximum 24 hours, unless otherwise instructed on an additional sign. Saturday and Sunday no time limit.
Parking spot, you may park here for a maximum of 12 hours unless something else on an additional sign
Parking spot, you may park here for a maximum of 6 hours unless something else on an additional sign

Honk the horn and steer for the animals front in order to scare it from crossing roads in the future

questions.explanation: A moose seldom change direction. It's like a tank, it just rolls on. So we aim for the back and hope it gets out of the way. A deer can change direction so that trick doesn't work with them.

questions.question_text: How many kilograms can a fully grown swedish moose weigh at the most?

options.text: 700 kilograms
950 kilograms
150 kilograms
1.030 kilograms is the swedish moose record from 1935

questions.explanation: Around 700 kilograms if it's a big bull. Also, a moose is like a mouse trap for cars - the long legs put the weight high above. At a collision, you will smash the legs, getting the moose over the hood, in your lap through the windshield.

questions.question_text: You have collided with a wild boar. The boar is nowhere to be seen. Should you step out and mark the place with an orange paper strip for the regulators and the police?

options.text: Yes, but not there! I stay in the car, I drive up 200 meters and mark that place, and make sure that I tell the police I marked it 200 meters up to be sure not to get injured by the boar if it's still alive.
Yes, Boars must be marked out where they got hit.
Yes, the animals are more afraid of us than we are of them, no risk here.
No, I don't have to mark out anything since boars are tough. It will probably walk it off.

questions.explanation: A boar is a menace once it's pissed off or scared. They have tusks the size of knives and are quite fast. Stay in the car, or drive away if possible and stop further up the road to mark the spot of collision for the wildlife regulation officer.

questions.question_text: Where is the risk of wildlife greater?

options.text: On a countryroad with a stream, river or lake on one side and young low-growing forest on the other
Close to cornfields
On highways in the north of Sweden
On gravel roads close to mountains

questions.explanation: Wild animals need nutrition and water and safe places. Watch out for those places as you drive, especially in dusk and dawn, that's when most wildlife seek food and water so they move around more.

questions.question_text: This sign warns for wildlife, specifically for swedish moose. How should it affect your driving when passing this road sign?

options.text: I slow down and check the sides of the road more frequent, mentally prepared to brake if a moose or another wild animal suddenly appears on the road in front of me
I place the car slightly more to the right side of the road, in order to give the wild animal more road if they approach, since mooses are large animals
I turn my headlights on and lower my gear to make more engine sound, so that the moose may hear and se me more clearly
I turn on my phone camera and am prepared to film the moose

questions.question_text: You collide with this animal. What should you do now?

options.text: Provided that my car can still be driven, I should get out of there about 100 meters or so, and there I should mark the spot with something and call the police so that they can send a regulator to handle it. I also call my insurance company.

I have to get out of my car before I proceed driving and make sure that the animal is not injured, or if it's injured I have to make sure that it doesn't suffer. I must also call the insurance company and report that I have had an accident.
I have to call a hunter to find and kill the animal if it's injured. I must also call the car company and report the accident.
I have to go to the hospital to have a check up to make sure I'm okay.

questions.explanation: You do not, and I repeat NOT get out of the vehicle after colliding with a wild boar. They may attack and they can be ferocious. Drive away if possible, mark up the place for the wildlife regulators further up the road, call the police and insurance company from there. DON'T STEP OUT THERE.

questions.question_text: You collide with this animal. What should you do now?

options.text: Provided that my car can still be driven, I should get out of there about 100 meters or so, and there I should mark the spot with something and call the police so that they can send a regulator to handle it. I also call my insurance company.

I have to get out of my car before I proceed driving and make sure that the animal is not injured, or if it's injured I have to make sure that it doesn't suffer. I must also call the insurance company and report that I have had an accident.
I have to call a hunter to find and kill the animal if it's injured. I must also call the car company and report the accident.
I have to call a veterinarian.

questions.explanation: You do not, and I repeat NOT get out of the vehicle after colliding with a bear. They may attack and they can be ferocious. Drive away if possible, mark up the place for the wildlife regulators further up the road, call the police and insurance company from there. DON'T STEP OUT THERE.

questions.question_text: You are about to collide with this animal. What should you do now?

options.text: I brake as hard as I can, hold it and steer towards the rear end of the animal.
I brake as hard as I can, hold it and try to hold a steady course in my lane
I braked hard and aim for the center of the animal
I duck and cover under my steering wheel and brake hard

questions.explanation: Moose has a tendency to keep running in the same direction, they are not as agile as a roe deer or a hare. So if they decide to cross the street, they will in most cases do just that, regardless of you.

questions.question_text: You collide with this animal. What should you do now?

options.text: I stop the car, put on hazard lights, go out and see if the animal is injured or dead or if it kept running. If it kept running, I mark the place where it was last seen. If it's injured, I should end the animals suffering if I can. If it's dead, I draw it off the road. I must always call the police.
I stop the car, reverse and aim for the head to make sure the animal is not suffering anymore. Then I proceed driving to a car mechanic for a checkup.
I don't have to do anything, if the car is fine and the animal is dead, I may proceed.
I must call my insurance company

questions.explanation: Roe deers are fast and they are pack animals. Where there is one, there will surely be others close by. The duty to call the police is absolute if I collide with the following species: Roe deer, moose, wild boar, fallow deer, raindeer, red deer, otter, bobcat or Lynx, wolf, bear, eagle, wolverine or mouflon sheep.

questions.question_text: Certain species of wildlife must always be reported to the police if you collide with them, even if they are dead. Which ones?

options.text: Roe deer, moose, wild boar, fallow deer, raindeer, red deer, otter, bobcat or Lynx, wolf, bear, eagle, wolverine or mouflon sheep
All collisions with dogs, cats, cattle, horses and larger birds like swans or cranes must always be reported to the swedish Wildlife Regulation Agency
Raindeers, since they are both wildlife and indigenous Sapmi cattle
Only a collision with wildlife predators must be reported to the police.

questions.explanation: These species are to be reported, basically any predators vulnerable status, plus anything bigger than a roe deer.

questions.question_text: How many collisions between vehicles and moose happens every year in Sweden?

options.text: Between 5000 and 6000 kollisions with moose every year
Between 500 and 600 kollisions with moose every year
Between 50 and 60 kollisions with moose every year
Between 800 and 850 kollisions with moose every year

questions.explanation: 5000+ collisions and only about 10 lethal accidents every year. We are getting better at driver awareness and the construction of safer cars!

questions.question_text: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Recommended speed, the numbers may vary, here it's recommended 50 km/h
Temporary maximum speed, the numbers may vary, here it's 50 km/h
Recommended lowest speed, the numbers may vary, here it's recommended no lower speed than 50 km/h
Temporary distance to others, the numbers may vary, here it's recommended 50 meters to the car in front of you

questions.explanation: Usually this road sign is put at accidents, risky situations, constructions on road or similar. You don't have to but recommended means it's a good idea.

questions.question_text: It's a foggy morning on the country road and you have low visibility. How do you proceed?

options.text: I reduce my speed
I turn on my full beam so I can see better
I drive slightly more to the right in my lane to create space to onward coming traffic
I drive close to the car in front so I don't lose them in the fog and they surprise me

questions.explanation: If your vision is poor due to wather or obscured view, slow down to by reaction time.

questions.question_text: If you are in a situation with a long and steep downhill, and your vehicle accelerate without any help from you due to gravity, What should you do?

options.text: I keep the speed under the speed limit and other than that, I use as much momentum as possible in order to save fuel. I also make sure to shift down so I can engine brake and not wear down the brakes.
I use 50% of throttle, I also shift the gear up to a higher gear in order to save fuel
I use the hilllholder to hold my current speed and proceeds
I keep a good lookout for police and enjoy the high speed

questions.explanation: If you have to choose in between traffic safety and environment - you always choose traffic safety. There are not many situations where this problem occurs, but when it does you always think safety first.

questions.question_text: You come to this traffic sign. The speed limit is 70 km/h. What does this road sign mean then?

options.text: It is recommended that I reduce my speed to 50 km/h temporarily
It is mandatory for me to follow this temporary speed limit of 50 km/h
Only vehicles with a weight of more than 50 tons may drive in this lane
In 50 meters there will be a new speed limit

questions.explanation: Recommended speed means something extra is happening. It can be a road construction, a higher risk for queues, or something else. It doesn't matter the reason  if you are recommended to lower your speed, consider doing just that. They don't put up those signs for fun, there is always a vaild reason.

questions.question_text: Which statement of these is true?

options.text: Country roads has a basic speed limit of 70 km/h unless there is a sign that says otherwise
You can use the parking brake to brake harder and come to a full stop sooner
You must always keep a snow shovel in the trunk during winter season in Sweden
Moped drivers must wear a helmet and a spine protection gear att all tiles when riding their moped

questions.explanation: The basic speed in rural areas in 50 km/h unless otherwise stated.

questions.question_text: What does the 50 sign on the vehicle mean?

options.text: Recommended speed, the numbers may vary, here it's recommended 50 km/h
This vehicle is only allowed to go maximum 50 km/h
Maximum speed limit here is not allowed to be higher than 50 km/h
In 50 meters, there will be a road construction

questions.explanation: If the speed sign is black and rectangular, it means recommended speed. The probation sign, normally called a speed limit sign, is round and in the shape of a red circle with a yellow background.

questions.question_text: What information does this sign deliver?

options.text: It's a public road and it's 23 kilometer to the goal
The road 23 to the right will take you to the city of Nyköping
Nyköping is to the right here and it's 23 mil there (a swedish mil is not a mile, it's 10 kilometers)
Nyköping will take about 1 hour by car

questions.explanation: Blue direction sign means public road. Green direction sign means motorway or highway. Yellow direction sign means property road.

questions.question_text: What is the authority of a traffic controller?

options.text: They have the same right as a police to use police signs to regulate traffic in order to ensure a transport arrives safely with minimum disturbance to traffic flow
They have the right to search vehicles and withdraw a licence just as a police officer
They have no authority other than a regular driver, only difference is that their vehicle shows us where the wide transport lorry is and warns us for that
They may claim your vehicle for their needs but you have the right to demand a written receipt

questions.explanation: They may regulate traffic as a police and you are to oblige their instructions, but they are not police officers per se. They have a different purpose.

questions.question_text: Are you allowed to break a formation of military vehicles on any road?

options.text: No
Yes, if the gap in between the vehicles are more than 100 meters, since it's not a formation anymore
Yes, as long as I do not hinder the soldiers
Yes, but only if I can do so without any danger or risk occurs

questions.explanation: You must never break a military formation. Not vehicles, not marching soldiers, never.

questions.question_text: Engine braking is quite a concept in order to save fuel and get a smoother drive, but how do you actually do it?

options.text: I take my foot pressure off of the gas pedal early, pressing the brake pedal just enough to ignite the brake lights, and let the speed slowly decrease
I press down the clutch and roll freely to save fuel
I shift the gear to a lower gear and let the engine slow the vehicle down, 5 to 4, 4 to 3, 3 to 2 and 2 to 1st gear
I use the parking brake to control my speed

questions.explanation: Engine brake is usually done at engine laps of at least 1500 rpm, more often than not it can be faster. So no need to change the gear. Just release the gas pedal and slowly let the speed go down!

questions.question_text: When driving on a high speed road, some things are prohibited. What is the correct alternative here?

options.text: It is not allowed to reverse
It is not allowed to overtake several vehicles at the same time
You may not drive slower than 80 in this road
You are allowed to drive maximum 140 km/h in certain stretches of high speed road in Sweden

questions.explanation: Think about consequences. What would be the outcome if someone reversed at a road where others drive maybe 100-120 km/h? That would be quite dangerous.

questions.question_text: If you find yourself driving towards the wrong goal on the motorway - what is correct?

options.text: I must exit at an exit, find the entrance ramp in the opposite direction and take it
