I make a U-turn but first make sure that nobody is behind me
I use a bus stop
I turn around in one of the openings in the fence where there are lines

questions.explanation: A motorway has no oncoming traffic. If you make a U-turn or use a bus stop, the traffic is coming towards you from the wrong direction. You must first get to the other side of the fence, and openings are for special vehicles.

questions.question_text: You are driving on a motorway with 3 lanes in your direction - are you allowed to overtake and pass several cars at once on such a road?

options.text: Yes
No, I have to overtake them one at a time
Yes, if they are all cars. If it's a lorry or trailer or a bus, I must do them one at a time
No

questions.explanation: In this situation you have no oncoming traffic so it's perfectly okay to overtake several vehicles of any kind.

questions.question_text: What is the colour of the road signs that tells you it's a motorway?

options.text: Green
Yellow
Blue
White

questions.explanation: E4, E18, E20... they are all green. I'm sure you have seen them sometime?

questions.question_text: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Road tax station coming up. A camera will registrate my licence plate and send me the bill
Tax station for vehicles coming up. I must be prepared to pay for the usage of road
Cash free zone, make sure you have money on your credit card
Road tax station coming up. I must be prepared to pay with cash

questions.explanation: Automatically, the system will registrate you and send you a bill. This is not always active though, it depends on during which hours and where you are driving, but if you don't feel like paying make sure you choose another route or other hours.

questions.question_text: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Tunnel. The number states how long this tunnel is
Tunnel, the number states how far until the tunnel begins
Tunnel, no lorries allowed here
Tunnel, all vehicles must make sure that they have paid the tunnel fee before entering

questions.explanation: There are different tunnel categories depending on sensitivity, road usage and how many lives nearby. The numbers state how long the tunnel is.

questions.question_text: If you are going to exit the motorway to the right, which alternative is the best one?

options.text: I choose the furtherest land to my right, I check around me 200 meter before the exit, making sure I don't have a motorcycle or something to my right side, I indicate right, drive off on the exit as soon as I can and then reduce my speed, in order to not hinder on the motorway
I reduce my speed in the right lane but wait to change, to let others pass me from behind so I don't hinder others
I slowly turn to the right, no blinkers needed.
I slow down in good time before my exit since I don't know which speed is appropriate after the exit

questions.explanation: Traffic is meant to flow. We must strive to not become a hindrance to others. Motorway exits are built for you to be able to keep your speed until you are at the off ramp.

questions.question_text: What is the maximum speed limit of a lorry towing a trailer on any road in Sweden?

options.text: 80 km/h
90 km/h
70 km/h
100 km/h

questions.explanation: 80 km/h. This is due to braking distances and fuel consumption. The faster we go, the more air is mmoved and the air resistance increases, costing more fuel.

questions.question_text: What is the maximum speed limit of a lorry on the motorway in Sweden?

options.text: 90 km/h if the lorry has modern pneumatic suspension
70 km/h
100 km/h
120 km/h

questions.explanation: If the lorry is a modern lorry and the road has 90 km/h or more as a speed limit, lorries can go maximum 90 km/h as long as they are not towing a trailer.

questions.question_text: What is true when you have seen this sign on your road?

options.text: You may not drive a tractor on this road
You can only reverse on the hard shoulder
You may only stop to pick up passengers or load or unload your vehicle, but you are not allowed to park
Be prepared for roundabouts or intersections

questions.explanation: Tractors are too slow for motorways and are therefore prohibited. A tractor on a motorway is an insurance claim just waiting to happen.

questions.question_text: Are you allowed to pick up passengers, hitchhikers for example, on a motorway?

options.text: No, I must not stop on a motorway
Yes, if it's on the entrance lane
Yes, if it's broad enough and I put my blinkers on and I do not disturb other traffic
No, hitchhiking is not allowed and I make myself an accessory

questions.explanation: Don't stop on the motorway unless the traffic situation demands it. Picking up passengers does not give you a valid reason, they are not allowed to be there in the first place. If their car broke down, let a professional handle it on the motorway! It's too unsafe.

questions.question_text: How should you read this sign?

options.text: In 100 meters, I have a road tax station camera
If I proceed, I have to pay 100 to pass the road tax station
The coming 100 meters will be under police camera coverage
Prohibited to use a camera the next 100 meters

questions.explanation: Sometimes this sign also tells in between which hours the toll of the road applies.

questions.question_text: What are the hearing requirements of driving a car in Sweden?

options.text: None whatsoever, you can be completely deaf and drive!
You must have 50% capacity for at least one ear
You have to have a score of at least 68,8 percentile in both ears, or succeeding at least 80,1 percentile on one ear
You must have perfect hearing.

questions.explanation: We do sometimes use our hearing when driving, to listen for signal horns or strange sounds from our vehicle, but 90% of impressions needed for driving is eye sight.

questions.question_text: When can you more probably experience an optical illusion?

options.text: Onward-coming car has a broken light so I mistake it for a motorcycle in the dark
In the woodlands of Sweden, where the elves has been dancing and the fog is thick
If the windshield is too clean and it starts to rain
If you have had too many cinnamon buns to your coffee

questions.explanation: This is not a joke. Keep your margins to onward coming traffic, and even if it's okay to hope for the best - always be prepared for the worst. A motorcycle weighs a couple of 100 kilograms. It demolishes a car at a frontal collision on a country road.

questions.question_text: Speed blindness is a thing. Can we do something to prevent it?

options.text: Yes, we can look to the side of us in short glimpses. This way we will see how fast the car is really going. Also, check your speed at the speed meter!
No, once it has occurred it is too late. You have to take a break from driving a few minutes or so.
Yes, keep your eyes as far up the road as you can
No, but speed blindness is not illegal so it does no harm

questions.explanation: Speed blindness occurs when we have been driving a certain speed for a long period of time. The eyes will adjust to this and look further from the car, which is good to recognise risks. It does however put our sense of speed a bit off when we slow down and follow a slower pace.

questions.question_text: What is periferal view and how much of what the eyes see is that?

options.text: Periferal view is everything we see that is not what we focus our gaze on, the blurry part around our focus. We use it to discover movements from the sides and it makes up for 98% of what we see.
Periferal view is the part of our eyesight that sees colours, it's 70%
Periferal view is the focus part of what we look at, it's roughly 2% of what we see.
Periferal view is used to look at long distances, it makes up for 33% of what we see.

questions.explanation: 98% or so is periferal view, it helps us see movements, what comes from the sides. Only 2% is the sharp area of our view that we focus in on.

questions.question_text: How does driving in a tunnel affect your visual ability?

options.text: The risk of tunnel vision is increased
Your visibility is improved due to the tunnel lights
You will drive slower due to Carpaths tunnel phenomenon
Your side mirrors will have clearer visibility

questions.explanation: The brain kind of shuts down the periferal view when you get tunnel seeing. Check your surroundings and be aware.

questions.question_text: What would affect reaction time the most?

options.text: Fatigue, you react much slower when you are really tired
Age. Young people react much faster in traffic
Your speed.
Your brake servo injector

questions.explanation: Human factor is the number one risk to consider. Stay alert when driving!

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true?

options.text: You as a driver are always responsible to keep such a distance margin to the vehicle in the front of you that you can stop safely if they should panic brake to a halt
You as a driver are always responsible if your vehicle malfunctions and you have to stop at the motorway
You as a learner are always responsible if you do not follow the tutors instructions and an accident occurs
You as a driver must make sure that everyone in your car use the seat belt

questions.explanation: You cannot stop others from driving too close to you from behond (tailgating) but you can and should keep your distance to the vehicle in front of you. 3 seconds in between is a good measure!

questions.question_text: If you drive in 100 km/h, how many meters do you drive in 3 seconds?

options.text: 83,3 meters
58,6 meters
Exactly 100 meters
125,1 meters

questions.explanation: Easy math! There are 60 seconds to a minute and there are 60 minutes to an hour. This means, there are 3600 seconds to 1 hour. Divide it and you get 100 000 meters (100 kilometers) divided by 3600 seconds to get the meters per second, now multiply it by 3 since the question was 3 seconds, and you get 83,3 meters per 3 seconds.

questions.question_text: What is the correct description of the concept of "Reaction distance"?

options.text: The distance which the vehicle travels from the moment the driver discovers a situation until the driver makes an action
The distance which the vehicle travels from the moment the driver discovers a situation until the vehicle has stopped completely
The distance which the vehicle travels from the moment the driver starts to brake until the vehicle has stopped completely
The time it takes for the driver to react to a stimuli of either visual, auditive or other, until the vehicle is cleared of danger

questions.explanation: Reaction distance is the distance you move before your brakes begin to brake. Reaction distance added to the brake distance equals the stop distance. First you must react and hit the brakes. Then you have to actually brake, and once the vehicle is standing still? That is called stop distance.

questions.question_text: You are driving on a motorway from Falun to Hedemora, a journey of 50 kilometers. How much time can you save by going 110 km/h instead of 90 km/h?

options.text: Roughly 6 minutes. The journey will take either 27 minutes and 20 seconds in 110 km/h or 33 minutes and 20 seconds in 90 km/h
Roughly 10 minutes. The journey will take either 25 minutes and 30 seconds in 110 km/h or 35 minutes and 30 seconds in 90 km/h
Roughly 15 minutes. The journey will take either 23 minutes and 40 seconds in 110 km/h or 38 minutes and 20 seconds in 90 km/h
Roughly 17 minutes. The journey will take either 20 minutes and 10 seconds in 110 km/h or 37 minutes and 15 seconds in 90 km/h

questions.explanation: To get the math done right, learn this formula: Time = Distance divided by Speed. In any case, you don't save a lot of time after the speeds you are calculating are over 70 km/h, but it's more risky. Better late than never!

questions.question_text: In which of these situations should you not use your rear fog lights?

options.text: When driving during the daytime and it rains a little bit
When it's a heavy snowfall in darkness
When it's foggy and dark
When it's foggy and dusk

questions.explanation: Fog light. The answer is in the name. Use this quite strong lamp only during such circumstances when others may not see you otherwise, such as fog, snowfall or really heavy rain.

questions.question_text: You are driving during dark hours at a country road and see the lights around the curve from oncoming traffic. At what distance do you switch your headlights to dipped beam?

options.text: When their light and my light together light up the road in between us
When I see the other vehicle
When I pass the other vehicle

questions.explanation: With the dipped beam you can only see a person in dark clothing or a wild animal 25 meters ahead or so, but if you keep your light on longer, you can see much further. However, don't blind the other car driver! Switch in just the right time.

questions.question_text: We must not blind the driver of the other car, but why? What is the common basic main traffic rule that you can apply in this situation?

options.text: A trafficant must never be an unneccessary hindrance or disturbance to other trafficants
A driver must never use full beam while oncoming traffic is within 300 meters
A driver must always give way to others
A trafficant must never drive if the traffic light is red

questions.explanation: The basic traffic rule, which is one of the most important traffic rules to obey, states that: A trafficant must in order to avoid traffic accidents act accordingly and with enough consideration to the situation at hand, that a trafficant must never unneccessary hinder or disturb other trafficants and show proportionate consideration to seniors, children and trafficants with a handicap.

questions.question_text: At what distance can you see a reflecting vest worn by a pedestrian, if you drive with dipped beam in darkness?

options.text: 125 meters
50 meters
25 meters
200 meters

questions.explanation: With your dipped beam you will see them about 125 meter away. If you have your high beam, it will be about 300 meters. If the person has dark clothes and no reflecting clothing, it might be as short of a distance as 25 meters before you discover them.

questions.question_text: High beam and dipped beam is used depending on the situation. In case you have oncoming traffic in this situation, which driver can keep the high beam a little longer? You or the oncoming driver?

options.text: The oncoming drivers beam will not be facing me straight on, since it's uphill and left curve for them, so it will not blind me directly. My light however, coming downhill and right curve, will blind the driver sooner.
I will be able to have my high beam on all the way, since the oncoming traffic will not be able to do anything about it.
We can both have the high beam on all the way.
They must switch to dipped beam before me, since their light will blind me otherwise. I can keep it on a bit longer since my beam will not be aimed straight for the driver.

questions.explanation: Keep a lookout for the beam of oncoming traffic in this situation, you will see it before you see the car.

questions.question_text: What would you say would be the right choice in this situation?

options.text: Turn on the high beam, adapt speed to the line of sight. It's dark outside, no street lights and no buildings, so it might be risk of wildlife as well.
I should drive 30 km/h here to have time to react if something unexpected happens, due to the poor visibility.
If I can't see them, then they can't see me either. I lower the speed since I cannot see very far, put my fog lights on to see better and so that others see me.
I turn my dipped beam on and stay closer to the side of the road.

questions.explanation: This is actually a maximum 80 km/h country road. This is how little you see in that speed with dipped beams.

questions.question_text: You are driving at night at a 70 km/h country road. Your full beam is on. In the distance, you see something reflecting your light. How do you proceed?

options.text: I lower my speed, put my foot on the brake and drive with more attention
I accelerate to make a noise with my engine to scare off wildlife
I aim for the object in order to collect my light towards it so that I can see better what it is
I turn my dipped beam on and stay closer to the side of the road.

questions.explanation: Speed shortens the reaction window - the faster you go, more will happen before you make a decision.

questions.question_text: A vehicle is coming on and they have forgotten to turn their dipped beam on. Where do you look in order not to become blinded by their lights?

options.text: I look a bit beyond the oncoming car and to the right side of the road
I look at the car in between the lights
I look to the left of the oncoming car
I look the driver straight in the eyes and slowly shake my head in disapprovement

questions.explanation: Your yellow spot in your eye, which is responsible for 1-2 percent of everything that you see, is your direct gaze and focus. Place the light away from it and also look to the right side of the road.

questions.question_text: Some modern cars are equipped with automatic light which activates depending on daylight or dusk. What might be the risk of always driving with your automatic lights on?

options.text: My positioning lights to the rear might not turn on, even though the circumstances might make rear lights beneficial (heavy rain or snow etc.)
It requires extra electricity which means the car will use more fuel to power the charging of the battery, hence bad for the environment
If the circuit is closed in automatic setting, all lights die at once and not just one lamp
Greater risk for a fire in the engine compartment due to the circuits passing through the light box

questions.explanation: The automatic light function is relatively new to Sweden, even if the technique has been around for some time. Since the law changed from "lights on even during midday", there has been a significant increase in the number of accidents when a vehicle hit another vehicle from behind.

questions.question_text: What should you do if you get tired while driving?

options.text: I switch places with someone less tired who has a driver licence, or I stop for a power nap if I'm alone.
I turn up the volume and sing along with the radio
I stop somewhere for a quick burger and fries and use the restroom
I lower the windows to get some fresh air

questions.explanation: How often have you heard "Sorry about my poor driving, I'm a bit drunk"? Not that often, right? But have you ever heard someone say "You look tired, should I drive?" More often. Don't drive if you are too tired!

questions.question_text: "Micro-sleep", which is the correct description?

options.text: A few seconds of unaware sleep
10-15 minutes of shallow sleep
Also called R.E.M. sleep, the deep sleep in between dreams
The light sleep where we have dreams and nightmares

questions.explanation: Ever been so tired you nod and wake up with a quick breath? Micro-sleep. Don't continue the drive without rest!

questions.question_text: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: No studded tyres allowed on any engine driven vehicle except for electric bicycles and mopeds class II
It means no studded tyres allowed for all vehicles
It means no dirtbikes allowed
It means high risk of a flat tyre

questions.explanation: There is a lot being done to improve the air quality and clean air benefits us all. Studded tyres may cause more super-small particles and dust, so therefore it is limited in areas with a dense population.

questions.question_text: Stress is always bad in traffic. Correct?

options.text: No. Some stress can have a positive effect on your awareness and level of focus and reaction time.
Yes. Always keep your calm and drive slower than all the others, plan your drive so that you have extra time
Yes, all stress is bad for the health and the body.
No. Stress is always good, it helps you perform your best and you cannot relax when you drive

questions.explanation: Positive stress, which is a bit of it but no more than you can handle, is actually helping us out! Too much is always too much and in general, it's best to stay calm and drive safe.

questions.question_text: If the temperature would drop during the night from -3 C down to -11 C, does this affect the risks of your morning drive to work in any way?

options.text: Such a temp drop would risk that a road which has been salted would refreeze and become quite slippery
No difference
It's safer if it's colder since the winter tyres grip increases, they are made for colder weather
It might lower the tyre pressure since air shrinks when it gets colder and this temp drop would reach a dangerous low tyre pressure due to that

questions.explanation: Salted roads help against ice, but only down to a certain degree. Salt water can also freeze and then it becomes slippery again.

questions.question_text: It's bleak swedish midwinter and you forgot to put the heater on, so the car is now cold as you drive away. At which temperature does the catalyst converter function best?
questions.explanation: The working temperature is 400-600 C, so it will take a while for you if it's -40 C outside which can happen in the north of Sweden. That is, if the car even starts...

questions.question_text: At which part of a car journey is it most likely that you fall asleep if you are tired?

options.text: At the end of the journey.
Midway through the journey.
In the beginning of the journey.
Doesn't matter, I just drink some coffee.

questions.explanation: Most people drown seeing the shoreline. Same is true for driving tired - we relax and think we are there, but we're not. Don't relax until you have turned the engine off!

questions.question_text: How can you best counter slippery road conditions?

options.text: Keep a lower speed and use good tyres for the season
Use tyres with at least 1,6 mm tread at summer and 3 mm at winter, drive according to the speed limit.
Always drive a bit slower than the speed limit
Use a 4x4 wheeled car

questions.explanation: The number one thing to do is to slow down, the second thing is good tyres.

questions.question_text: Which situation is most likely the most slippery in the winter?

options.text: Intersections, when I take off from standing still
Downhill
Uphill
Curves

questions.explanation: The intersection is where many cars have come to a stand still and many has also polished the snow into ice from trying to take off. This creates extra slippery conditions.

questions.question_text: You are getting sleepy during a night time drive. What of the following can you do to best counter this and stay awake until you're home?

options.text: Stop and sleep for 20 minutes
Turn the volume up and sing along with the radio
Drink lots of coffee, I will get both caffeine and the need to pee which will keep me awake
Roll down the windows

questions.explanation: Power nap is more effective than any other of the methods here. However, why not do all of them?

questions.question_text: In between which hours does most traffic accidents involving tiredness/fatigue happen?

options.text: 3 am - 5 am
11 pm - 02 am
6 am - 11 am
4 pm - 6 pm

questions.explanation: These are the "wolf hours", where most people are the most tired. Make sure that you are rested if you ahve to drive at these hours, and be prepared that everyone you meet might be tired.

questions.question_text: Your car shows this symbol in the dashboard. What is the correct answer?

options.text: I immediately stop the car at a safe place, turn off the engine and tow the car to a mechanic
It's a symbol that means I have to fill up more brake fluid
I don't need to do anything since it's only a circuit for the rear window heater
I have to put my seatbelt on

questions.explanation: If the engine oil level is low, the engine gets hot really fast and without the oil to lubricate it, it might never work again if you don't stop driving right now.

questions.question_text: This symbol lights up on your dashboard. What does it mean?

options.text: Airbag system is malfunctioning
The sun shield is getting worn
The fan needs service
Night vision system is malfunctioning

questions.question_text: This symbol lights up on your dashboard. What does it mean?

options.text: Fuel level is getting low
Fuel pump is not working
The reserve fuel tank is deactivated
Phone is disconnected

questions.question_text: This symbol lights up on your dashboard. What does it mean?

options.text: The level of engine oil is danger low - stop at a safe place and turn the engine off as soon as possible
The car needs lubrication on the brake system
The engine oil is too hot, turn the AC to lowest temperature and drive to a mechanic.
You have to refill the brake oil.

questions.question_text: This symbol lights up on your dashboard. What does it mean?

options.text: Anti-lock Braking System
All-wheel Braking Signal
All-wheel Braking System
Anti Brake System

questions.question_text: This symbol lights up on your dashboard. What does it mean?

options.text: The alternator is not functioning properly
You have to change the car battery
You have to change the distilled water in the car battery
Your electric car needs to be charged

questions.question_text: This symbol lights up on your dashboard. What does it mean?

options.text: Different symbols of brakes, the one with the P is parking brake so I probably forgot to release it.
Brakes are getting worn, I must change the brake violets.
Check the parking sensors
The automatic brake system is malfunctioning

questions.question_text: As you start up your car and get ready to drive off, the Airbag warning lamp is lit up, then after 2 seconds or so, it's turned off again. Which one is the proper alternative?

options.text: You proceed to drive as if nothing happened
I can drive for now but I should have it checked out by a professional
Stop the car immediately and don't drive until this error has been fixed
I turn off the engine, wait for 2 minutes and try again

questions.explanation: It's just the system checking for all the sensors to function properly, completely normal. Drive on!

questions.question_text: This symbol lights up on your dashboard. What does it mean?

options.text: You have your full beam head lights on
You have your dipped beam turned off
Fog lights are on
A lamp is broken in the front

questions.question_text: This symbol lights up on your dashboard. What does it mean?

options.text: The engine oil temperature is danger high, put AC in hottest and full fan, drive to a safe place, stop the engine and let it cool down
Low level of motor oil, refill as soon as you can
AC is too hot, put it in low temp and wait for the lamp to go away
Your gearbox has lost a circuit

questions.question_text: This is a battery symbol, but what does it actually mean?

options.text: It means that the battery for some reason is not charging
It means that the battery needs to be replaced
It means you must charge the battery in your electric car
It means the battery is fully charged

questions.explanation: The battery can be without charge for many reasons, so when you check why, make sure that you measure if power comes from the alternator/generator as well as checking the battery.

questions.question_text: This symbol lights up on your dashboard. What does it mean?

options.text: Windshield wash fluid is low
Leakage in the engine compartment
Coolant system is down
Time to switch the wipers

questions.question_text: This symbol lights up on your dashboard. What does it mean?

options.text: Your fog light is activated
Your tunnel lights are activated
Your reversing lights are broken or deactivated
You must change the registration plate lamps

questions.question_text: This symbol lights up on your dashboard. What does it mean?

options.text: Something is probably the matter with the delivery of fuel, the sparkplugs or the oxygen. Keep driving for now, but get a mechanic to check it when you can.
The engine is too hot, stop at once. Yellow is a warning, red is a malfunction!
The carburator needs cleaning, the engine doesn't cool off as it should
The car has low level of power torque, change the motivator

questions.question_text: What is false about the warning symbols on your dashboard?

options.text: Red warning always means you have to stop and turn the engine off
In the manual for the car I can find what all the symbol means
Blue means that the function is on
If the oil lamp is turned on, I should stop the engine from going as soon as it's possible in a safe way

questions.explanation: The parking brake for instance, can be red. If that is turned on, you must only disengage it, no need to turn the engine off in that situation.

questions.question_text: Summer tyres and winter tyres have a tread dept by law. Winter tires needs to have at least 3 mm left of tread debt, but what about summer tires?

options.text: 1,6 mm
1,0 mm
5 mm
2,2 mm

questions.explanation: 1,6 mm. 1,6 mm. 1,6 mm. Memorise it!

questions.question_text: Where can you find out which tyre measurements you should have for your car?

options.text: In the cars instruction manual
In the registration papers of the car (blue one)
In the registration papers of the car (yellow one)
On the tyres

questions.explanation: You can find it in the instruction manual or you can ask a professional tyre expert. Do not use other measurements than the ones designed for your car, it can mess with speed meter, grip on the road, engine presatnda and other things too. Go with what your manufacturer recommends!

questions.question_text: Typical! You have a flat tyre... Luckily, you have a spare in the trunk. Does it have to be studded if the other tyres on your car are studded?

options.text: No, there is no such requirement
Yes, all tyres on the vehicle must be the same regarding studded or not
Yes, but I may retract all the studs from my other tyres with a wrench
The only demand is that the studded tyres must be replaced as soon as I can get the car to a tyre firm

questions.explanation: The spare tyre is only supposed to get you out of there and drive home, or to a mechanic, or any other place where you can fix the problem. Drive extra careful, and have the standard tyre fixed as soon as you can.

questions.question_text: Between which days of the year must your car have winter tyres in Sweden?

options.text: Between the 1st of December to the 31st of March, or if the road conditions are such that it's to be estimated as winter
Between the 16th of October to the 16th of April, but studded tyres only up until the last of February
Between 1st of November to the 1st of April
It depends where in Sweden, Skåne and Kiruna has quite different rules due to the different seasons and when the snow falls

questions.explanation: You are always allowed to have winter tyres, as long as they are not studded. It's highly recommended to drive season customized tyres though.

questions.question_text: Which tread pattern is legal to drive with on summer tyres?

options.text: 1,6 mm on the thinnest part of the pattern
2,0 mm on the middle of the tread pattern
3,0 mm on the thinnest part of the tread pattern
1,5 mm on the thinnest part of the tread pattern

questions.explanation: 1,6 mm for summer tyres, 3,0 mm for winter tyres. Memorise this!

questions.question_text: After changing or fixing a flat tyre, you should make sure the bolts are not shaken loose. After driving how long is it recommended that you check the bolts?

options.text: 50 kilometers or thereabout
After 100 kilometers
10 kilometers, or there about
Just after is enough, drive around the block and then check if they are still tight

questions.explanation: Tyres and wheels need a bit of time to settle, 50 kilometers is recommended by most companies. Be sure you don't tighten them too much or you might break them. Ask a pro if you are uncertain!

questions.question_text: Is tyre pressure an important thing?

options.text: Yes. Because if you have too low pressure, your grip will be less predictable, your tyres will be worn out sooner and also the fuel consumption will be higher, if tyre pressure is too high - you have less grip and you will feel every bump
Yes. Because low tyre pressure will increase the risk of tyre explosion, high pressure will cause a higher fuel consumption and decrease the maneuverability
Yes. High tyre pressure makes for a difference in speed meter value and actual speed, low tyre pressure will make the car suspension be more worn
Tyre pressure is only important to the point that the pressure is not so low that it's flat

questions.explanation: Tyre pressure is an exact science and very important for how the car will behave. Follow the manufacturers advise.

questions.question_text: Tyres have a pattern in order to move water and snow out of the way. What is the minimum requirement of tyre tread dept for winter tyres?

options.text: 3 mm
5 mm
1,6 mm
1,1 mm

questions.explanation: 3 mm for winter tyres and 1,6 mm for summer tyres. More is always better.

questions.question_text: You notice when you put on your winter tyres that 2 of your tyres are more worn than the other 2. Where do you put the good ones?

options.text: The rear axle
The front axle
It depends on wether my car is rear-wheel driven or front-wheel driven, since I should put them on the driven axle
Doesn't matter as long as I put them on the same axle

questions.explanation: Always put them in the rear axle, since your car is built to protect you best to the front. If you must collide with something, it's less dangerous to do it head on. For this, you need the car to not skid and turn during a panic brake.

questions.question_text: Can you change your sparkplugs yourself?

options.text: Yes, if you know how to and have the proper parts and tools
No, that is only for the mechanics since a malfunctioning sparkplug can be dangerous to change yourself
Yes, you just need a screwdriver, some sparkplugs and a good mood!
No, the engine has to be lifted

questions.explanation: If you don't know how to, you can learn and save a lot of money on not going to a mechanic. But it's perfectly safe to do yourself if you know how to. (and turn the ignition off)

questions.question_text: Which of the following alternatives is an accurate description of the most common place around the car referred to as the "blind spots"?

options.text: The areas diagonally behind the mirrors and to the side of the car
The area directly behind the car
The area over the car
The area in front of the car

questions.explanation: The blind spot is the area which we cannot see in the mirrors, where as we have to turn around and look over the shoulder to see what we have to the side of us and slightly behind us diagonally.

questions.question_text: Due to a poor battery, your car needs to get some help to start, using cables from another car battery. Is there anything you should consider extra regarding safety?

options.text: The battery may explode if I do it wrong
Electricity shock will cause a fatal cardiac arrest
I must make sure to attach the black cable to the black part of the battery and attach the red cable to the red part of the battery
As long as I use standard equipment it doesn't matter

questions.explanation: In some old car batteries that have lead and mild sulfuric acid in them, oxygen and hydrogen may be released during charging which is extremely flammable, and it may cause an explosion. Either do it outside or in a very well ventilated place.

questions.question_text: You have washed your car and it shines! What is important to do afterwards in order for the vehicle to be safe to drive?

options.text: I have to brake controlled a bit to ensure that the brakes are not wet and will take longer before they slow the car down efficiently
I have to check my tyres that they are not wet
I have to make sure that the car steering servo still functions
I must make sure that I apply new brake oil on my brake discs

questions.explanation: Water from the washing may still be on the brakes, so brake a bit to remove it. Good to go! And what a nice car you have, looks brand new!

questions.question_text: What is one of the latest requirements on a diesel car in Sweden?

options.text: Particle philtering
Catalyst converter
Needs an electric ADBlue heater
Must have exchangeable sparkplugs

questions.explanation: Diesel engines does not have sparkplugs, nor do they need any heater on the ADBlue tank. They have had catalyst converter for many years, but particle philtering is newer!

questions.question_text: Which one is more flammable, Diesel or petrol/gasoline?

options.text: Petrol/gasoline
Diesel
They are both just as flammable
That depends on the outside temperature

questions.explanation: Petrol/gasoline can self-ignite in hot weather. Diesel has a much higher ignition temperature.

questions.question_text: What must you always do after you have washed the car?

options.text: Brake
Throttle the gas pedal until engine reach 3000 rpm to remove water from the catalyst converter
Wipe off the tyres or drive a few kilometers to regain maximum grip
Check your brake fluid

questions.explanation: Water on the brakes might decrease the effect when you brake the first time after a car wash. Just brake mildly until you feel the brakes working properly.

questions.question_text: Your diesel car needs oil. Your friend offers you some of theirs, which they keep in the car for emergencies (smart friend!) What must you consider?

options.text: I have to make sure that the oil has the correct viscosity for my engine
I have to make sure that I change the oil filter as well
I must use only plant based engine oil in a electric car
I have to mix it 90-10 with AD-Blue if it's a diesel car

questions.explanation: You do not mix anything with engine oil. Ever. AD-Blue is a separate tank and is injected into the catalyst converter. The filter is good to exchange but not when this lamp is on. It does matter though, how thick or thin your oil needs to be for your engine, so viscosity is correct. An electric car has no engine oil…

questions.question_text: Your steering wheel is feeling awkward. When you turn it, it alters in between moving smoothly and moving really tough, with a lot of pressure, only to move easy again. What's the most likely reason?

options.text: Air in the steering servo system
The steering wheel needs to me greased with some lubrication
The water pump need to be changed
The tires are unevenly worn

questions.explanation: Hydraulic systems are generally not fond of air in the system. Consider if you get air in your blood veins. Not so good, right?

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not part of the security check of a car?

options.text: The seat belts
Signal horn
Brake servo
Coolant fluid level

questions.explanation: Believe it or not, in TSFS (2012:43) paragraph 14, seat belt is not a requirement for your security check! When you take the car to the test authorities, they will test them.

questions.question_text: Which lights on your car is allowed to use at the same time?

options.text: parking lights and dipped beam
Fog lights and dipped beam
There are no restrictions as long as your head light bulb has a value that is more than 5 W
dipped beam and extra head lights

questions.explanation: The dipped beam is only allowed to use at the same time as position lights and parking light.

questions.question_text: Due to a malfuntion in your vehicle, you have to drive much slower than the average speed on your current road stretch. Behind you there is a long queue. What is correct?

options.text: If possible, I find a good spot to overtake me and then I stop there to let the others pass
I signal to the others behind me that they may overtake once I see that the road ahead is clear
I drive slightly more to the left in my lane to create space to overtake me
I drive as I always do, in order to prevent any accidents I maintain my placement and make no changes

questions.explanation: One of the most important and all-covering traffic rules is the one that says "A trafficant must not unneccessarily hinder or disturb other trafficants", so don't be a jerk. Help one another in traffic!

questions.question_text: What is a risk behavior criteria to fall for negative peer pressure?

options.text: Low self-esteem and need for acceptance
High self-esteem and low empathy
Being a social person
Females are more prone than men to speed in traffic if their friends are in the car

questions.explanation: Low self-esteem makes one vulnerable for the expression of opinion from others. Don't do that. Trust your knowledge and your training! Drive as if your mother is watching!

questions.question_text: What is the most common intentional misconduct that people do in traffic?

options.text: Speeding
Using their cell phone while driving
Driving under the influence of alcohol
Driving too tired

questions.explanation: This is statistically the most common crime. We tend to over estimate our ability and under estimate the risks.

questions.question_text: What signifies impulsive drivers in their driving?

options.text: They do things first, and think about it after
They always drive too fast
They do not slow down in time, so they sometimes skid off of the road in curves
They honk their horn for no apparent reason

questions.explanation: To drive impulsive is dangerous. A predictable driver is a safe driver!

questions.question_text: Who will more likely give in to negative peer pressure?

options.text: Someone who wishes to impress or be accepted by the group
Someone who is confident in him or herself
A person with high social status
Males are more prone to drive slow if the situation demands it

questions.explanation: Low self-esteem makes one vulnerable for the expression of opinion from others. Be confident that you have the proper way to drive nailed, and don't be affected by others opinion.

questions.question_text: What would be an example of positive peer pressure?

options.text: When your friends asks you to slow down due to the weather conditions
When you encourage your friend to overtake a lorry in order to keep your schedule
When you have been drinking but don't tell your friends before you give them a ride
When your friends ask you to show what you can do

questions.explanation: This is more common with experienced drivers. Choose the less dangerous option, always.

questions.question_text: An immature driver is a bad driver. Which of the following examples is an example of immature attitude in traffic?

options.text: Another vehicle honks their horn at me from behind so I hit the brakes hard
I listen to baby shark while driving
I go to the side of the road and let others pass me, since they all seem to be in such a hurry
I slow down early before the turn so I can buy myself time to see a gap in traffic

questions.explanation: Leave your juvenile reactions and feelings at home. You are driving a car now. Adult up to the occation! Someone honks for no reason? This translates into "I HAVE SOME PERSONAL ISSUE AND I AM COMPENSATING!" Just ignore them. Let them live. There is no death penalty for honking.

questions.question_text: Deep or surface learning? Which one should we strive for?

options.text: Deep learning will give us a better understanding
Deep learning will slow us down when we need to react fast
Surface learning helps us understand different weather conditions better
Surface learning makes us good drivers on snow and ice

questions.explanation: Deep learning stays with you. Memorizing these answers will not. Make sure you understand what the purpose of the questions and answers are and answer from that perspective.

questions.question_text: Who will most likely not give in to negative peer pressure?

options.text: A person of high self confidence and no need for exterior confirmation
Persons with a low self-esteem
Persons with good knowledge of a car engine
Persons with a poor knowledge of a car engine

questions.explanation: Know yourself. Know your abilities and your limits. You cannot grow into a better driver or a better person or anything else if you ignore a risk and become another statistics in traffic victims. Stay alive, be smart.

questions.question_text: What does it mean that a driver is "impulsive"?

options.text: The driver acts without proper preparations and then realise eventual mistakes after
The driver seem to have an almost unnatural instinct for danger and is able to foresee risks better than the average driver
The driver reacts slower than the normal driver
The driver see risks where there aren't any

questions.explanation: 15% of the population is responsible for 50% of the traffic accidents that occur. These 15% are the risk takers, and it's more often than not a male in between 18-24 years of age who drives impulsively.

questions.question_text: What would be the legal consequence if you are caught going 45 km/h on a 30 km/h speed limit road?

options.text: Licence revoked and a fine
A lofty fee and a warning. Three warnings and they take your licence, if probation time is still valid
You have to do the theory test again
You will be prosecuted and go prison for 3-6 months

questions.explanation: A revoked licence is bad enough, but you will also get a fine, sometimes quite expensive. Drive according to the law. Also, if you kill someone it's a life sentence to deal mentally with that. Don't risk it.

questions.question_text: How should we all behave in traffic? Choose the statement that best reflects this.

options.text: Cooperate with others and adjust the speed according to the current situation
We slow down before passing a fountain
We give way even if the other car has a give way sign
Drive 10 km/h slower than asked to save fuel and be kind to the environment

questions.explanation: Drive defensive, risk aware and adjust accordingly.

questions.question_text: A person has been drinking alcohol the day before. What is the correct alternative?

options.text: The driver does not drive the day after to make sure not to drive under the influence
If the person calculates by bodyweight and age and time since the alcohol was consumed, the driver may drive if the math adds up
Take a brisk walk for about 45 minutes and see if you get dizzy. If not, just drive carefully.
Mix 1 teaspoon of baking soda into 1 liter of water, stir it, then drink it. Now it should be okay to drive.

questions.explanation: Tolerance can be a bad thing when applied to bad decisions. Never ever risk to drive under the influence. Nevermind the police or the lost money on a ticket - You have to live with what you've done if someone dies.

questions.question_text: What factor determines if a child should use an infant carrier, a rear-facing child safety seat, or a booster seat?

options.text: The length of the child
The weight of the child
The age of the child
The love for the child

questions.explanation: If a child is shorter than 135 centimeters, the driver is obliged to use equipment specialised for this. If the child is shorter than 140 centimeters, do not place in front of an airbag. Never place a specialised equipment such as an infant carrier in a seat with an active airbag.

questions.question_text: What is the limit in Sweden for aggravated drunk driving?

options.text: 1,0 per mille
0,5 per mille
0,2 per mille
0,0 per mille

questions.explanation: It should probably be 0,0 but it's 1,0. Ask yourself: Will alcohol make me a better driver no matter how much? No. So don't drink and then drive, leave the car for another day.

questions.question_text: You pick up a hitchhiker at the countryroad. The hitchhiker refuses to wear a seat belt. Can you as the driver be prosecuted?

options.text: Only if the hitchhiker is under the age of 15
Yes, first of all it's illegal to pick up hitchhikers and it's also my responsibility as a driver to make sure the seat belt is being used.
If the hitchhiker sits in the back, it's fine.
No, I never have any responsibility for my passengers.

questions.explanation: You as a driver are responsible for every passenger under the age of 15 to wear a seatbelt. If the hitchhiker is 15 or older, it's their own responsibility, true. But why drive on if you have a passenger at risk? Your car, your rules, wear a seatbelt or walk. Period.

questions.question_text: If you use your cellphone to answer a message and an accident occur, can you be legally processed for this?

options.text: Yes, if I held the device in my hand or if it affected my driving negatively in any way.
Yes, all usage of cell phones in the car is prohibited
No, but they will confiscate my phone
Yes, but only if it leads to an accident

questions.explanation: Pretty much anyone can cope a phone call while driving if the conversation is "Hi, it's me. Buy milk. Bye!" But what if the conversation is "It's close now, hurry to the hospital to say farewell", how good a driver are you then? Now it's not as easy, is it? Choose your phone calls, and use handsfree!

questions.question_text: You have to change the destination on your app in your phone. The phone is placed on a holder at the dashboard and is not held in your hand during this interaction. Is this allowed?

options.text: As long as it does not interfere with my driving I may do it, for example by voice command or by a passenger handling the phone app, but it's always safer to stop at a safe place and do it.
No. Phone usage is always prohibited while driving in traffic.
Yes, since I don't hold the phone in my hand it's not illegal.
Yes, if I have stopped at a red light anyway.

questions.explanation: It's not just about holding a phone, the law clearly states that you must pay attention while driving and if you divide your attention and focus, you must be sure that this does not affect your driving.

questions.question_text: What is true regarding the intake of precripted medicines and driving?

options.text: I must take responsibility for my ability to drive myself. I can find information about if the medicine impact driving skills or focus in the leaflet which comes with the medication.
I must consult a doctor to know for sure if the medicine might affect my driving
I can find a red warning triangle on the medications which can affect driving negatively
I have to check the active ingredients in the medication and compare it to the Trafikstyrelsen website, in order to know for sure

questions.explanation: It's always the driver who is responsible, so make sure berfore you drive that you read up in the leaflet if you experience any sense of being tired, unfocused, eyesight depression or any other symptoms which can cause your ability to drive!

questions.question_text: What is the correct statement about seat belts?

options.text: I as a driver of a car is responsible for everyone in the car under the age of 15 years old that they wear a seatbelt
I as a driver of a car is responsible for everyone in the car over the age of 15 years old that they wear a seatbelt
I as a driver of a car is responsible for everyone in the car under the age of 10 years old that they wear a seatbelt
I as a driver of a car is responsible for everyone in the car under the age of 18 years old that they wear a seatbelt

questions.explanation: 15 years of age is the legal age for Sweden. After a person has come of age of 15 years old, they are answering to the law themself. Still not fully adult since that age is 18 in Sweden, but you answer before the law yourself after 15 yars of age. However, if they don't wear the seatbelt you can stop the car and refuse to drive. Positive peer pressure and role models are good stuff!

questions.question_text: The airbag is active on the front passenger seat. What must you consider if you are driving a child passenger of 130 centimeters in a child seat?

options.text: I must place the child seat in the back seat and place the child passenger in the child seat
I must turn the child seat forward if I place it in the front seat
I must strap down the child seat with the airbag strap on the left side of the seat
Doesn't matter, the child is tall enough for airbag

questions.explanation: If the child is shorter than 135 centimeters, I must use the child seat. If the child is shorter than 140 centimeters, I must not place it in front of an active airbag, no matter which direction the child is facing. Put it in the back seat!

questions.question_text: What letter on your licence says that you are permitted to drive a lorry with a total weight of maximum 3500 kilograms?

options.text: B
AM
C1
C

questions.explanation: You are allowed to drive pickup trucks and such on your driving licence marked with a B (which means car), as long as the total weight doesn't exceed 3500 kilograms.

questions.question_text: You have promised a friend to help them today at lunch by driving your car with some small logs on the ribs on the roof of your car. While securing the logs on your roof, you notice the log will stick out behind the car about 80 centimeters. What is correct?

options.text: I should make it more visible with a small red light or a red flag of some sort
I don't have to mark my load since it's not pointing out more than 1,0 meters
I will only be driving in the daylight so no marking of the load is needed
I have to mark it out since all cargo that sticks out from the car has to be clearly marked, white to the front and red to the back, just like the lights of my car

questions.explanation: You must mark out your cargo if it sticks out from your car more than 1,0 meters, but also if the cargo is not clearly visible!

questions.question_text: You need to rent a 750 kg trailer at a gas station in Sweden. What must you as a driver make sure to check?

options.text: I must check that if my car has studded winter tyres, the trailer must also be equipped likewise
I need a B96 or BE licence to drive a trailer in the winter
I have to make sure that the trailer duomatic is functioning
If my tyres are not studded, the trailer tyres cannot be studded either

questions.explanation: Always have the best tyres the furtherest back of your vehicle combination. In this case you have to have studded tyres on the trailer if your car has studded tyres.

questions.question_text: If your attached 750 kg trailer has brakes, what is the maximum speed limit for you to drive with it?

options.text: 80 km/h
40 km/h loaded, 70 km/h unloaded
Depends on the road speed limit - I may never drive faster than 70 km/h
No speed limit for light trailers (750 kg or lower)

questions.explanation: It's the same as for a lorry with a trailer. Maximum 80 km/h if the trailer has brakes, even if it's a 100 km/h highway.

questions.question_text: What is the maximum gross weight allowed for a pickup for which a car licence is required?

options.text: 3500 kilograms
2500 kilograms
4250 kilograms
As long as it's just a pickup, I may drive it on my car licence no matter the weight

questions.explanation: Total weight may never be above 3500 kilograms if you are to drive it on your car driving licence, which means the gross weight (here and now) can also not superecede this weight.

questions.question_text: You are driving a caravan behind your car and with your extra mirrors, that is exactly 221 centimeters width, including its side-view mirrors. Are you permitted to drive past this sign?

options.text: No; the width of the vehicle, including its load and side-view mirrors, must not exceed the dimension specified on the sign
Yes; side-view mirrors are never included in the vehicle's width in the context of this prohibition sign
Yes, provided you fold in the side-view mirrors and drive very slowly past the obstacle
Yes; there is always an additional margin of 20 centimeters beyond what is stated on the sign

questions.explanation: Probation is probation. Also, remember that 2600 millimeters, or 260 centimeters, or 2,6 meters is the ABSOLUTE maximum width you may have, unless you wish to pay for an extra traffic transport leader...

questions.question_text: What does "total weight" mean when we speak of cars?

options.text: It is the maximum cargo weight plus the curb weight/also known as service wight
It is the weight that a car weighs right now
It is the total amount of cargo that a car can hold
It is the total weight that the vehicle transfers from the wheel axis to the road at a given moment

questions.explanation: Read more about the different definitions of weight. Total weight is written in the vehicle registration papers, it is the service weight plus maximum cargo weight.

questions.question_text: What does the gross weight of the vehicle mean?

options.text: It is the current static weight that is transfered from the wheels to the road at a given moment (So you need a scale to drive up on)
It is the maximum weight that the vehicle construction is built to handle
It is the maximum weight of cargo that a vehicle can carry according to swedish road standards
It is the weight of the vehicle with a driver included, all fluids filled, no cargo counted

questions.explanation: Gross weight is what the vehicle weighs, right here, right now.

questions.question_text: If you weigh 75 kilograms and your car has a service weight of 2200 kilograms and a total weight of 2800 kilograms, how much cargo can you carry in your car?

options.text: 600 kilograms, passengers included
675 kilograms, passengers included
675 kilograms, passengers excluded
When the other vehicle turn their lights off

questions.explanation: Service weight means a driver of 75 kilograms, all fluids and tools that came from the car factory with the car and spare tyre if such was included. Passenger weight is considered cargo weight.

questions.question_text: You have bought a caravan to hang behind your car, but the car doesn't have a hitch. Easy-peasy, you install one yourself! Are you now required to have a registration inspection performed of your work?

options.text: No
Yes, if it's a pickup or other light lorry but not otherwise
Yes, all vehicles that makes such a change that alters the performance of the vehicle must be inspected
Yes, if the hitch is built for a pull weight that exceeds 750 kilograms

questions.explanation: It used to be the case that an inspection was needed, but since 2013 they changed the rules and now you don't have to. You will however have the hitch inspected on your regular checkup! So make sure you do it right.

questions.question_text: It's bleak swedish midwinter. Are you allowed to tow your trailer if your car has studded tyres but the trailer does not?

options.text: No
Yes
Yes, it's the other way around that is prohibited
As long as the tread pattern is no less than 3 mm for winter tyres, it's okay

questions.explanation: The risk here is that your trailer comes up next to you if you brake hard. That is a most unpleasant experience and quite dangerous. Always make sure you consider safety first and foremost!

questions.question_text: Which of these trailers can you drive on a B licence (car) without breaking the law?

options.text: A trailer with a total weight of maximum 750 kilograms
A trailer with a total weight of maximum 500 kilograms
A trailer with a gross weight of 750 kilograms
A trailer with a gross weight of maximum 500 kilograms

questions.explanation: As long as the car can handle it according to its registration, you may drive a trailer with a total weight of 750 kilograms, or, if the car and the trailer can handle it according to their registrations, you may also tow a trailer that exceeds 750 kilograms as long as the total weight of both vehicles does not weigh more than 3500 kilograms.

questions.question_text: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: I cannot pass this sign if my vehicle is broader than 2,2 meters
I may not pass this sign if my vehicle is higher than 2,2 meters
I may not pass this sign if my vehicle weighs more than 2,2 metric tons
I may not pass this sign if my vehicle is longer than 2,2 meters

questions.explanation: The number of the sign states the allowed width of the vehicle.

questions.question_text: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: I cannot pass this sign if my vehicle is higher than 3,5 meters
I cannot pass this sign if my vehicle is broader than 3,5 meters
I may not pass this sign if my vehicle weighs more than 3,5 metric tons
I may not pass this sign if my vehicle is longer than 3,5 meters

questions.explanation: The number of the sign states the allowed height of the vehicle.

questions.question_text: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: I cannot pass this sign if my vehicle and/or trailer is longer than 20 meters
I cannot pass this sign if my vehicle is higher than 20 meters
I can only pass this sign if my pulling vehicle is shorter than 20 meters, but trailer is unaccounted for
My vehicle must be at least 20 meters long to be allowed on this road

questions.explanation: The number of the sign states the allowed length of the vehicle.

questions.question_text: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Minimum distance to the car in front of me is 50 meters after this sign
Maximum distance to the car in front of me is 50 meters after this sign
The exact distance to the car in front of me must be 50 meters after this sign
Medium distance to the car in front of me is 50 meters after this sign

questions.explanation: This sign is put up on roads that demands a greater distance in between vehicles. The numbers on the sign states the minimum distance, in this case 50 meters.

questions.question_text: Bridges has to be high enough so that a lorry or a bus or any other tall vehicle doesn't collide with it. How do we know if the bridge is high enough?

options.text: If the bridge is lower than 4,5 meters, a road sign for this bridge will be put up
All bridges in Sweden is 4,0 meters high at least, so all vehicles are built to fit under that
You must have special traffic escort leader car in front of you if you are higher than 4 meters
All bridges are higher than 5 meters and the highest allowed lorry is 4,7 meters, so it's never an issue

questions.explanation: 4,5 meters or you have to mark the bridge and warn with road signs. Lorries are seldom higher than that. In the rest of Europe, it's usually 4,0 meters.

questions.question_text: How wide maximum is a vehicle allowed to be on the road without the need for a special permit?

options.text: 2600 mm including cargo sticking out from the sides
2550 mm including mirrors and cargo
2700 mm including cargo
The vehicle itself must never be wider than 2450 mm, the cargo may exceed this for a maximum of 200 mm on each side

questions.explanation: 2600 millimeters, or 260 centimeters, is the maximum. If you are wider than this with cargo and everything else sticking out on the side, you need a special permit for wide load (swe = Bred last), special markings and probably a traffic controller escort.

questions.question_text: You are driving a high-roof small lorry where the highest point on the roof is 3,45 meters. The sign indicates 3,5 meters. What is the safest and most correct course of action here?

options.text: You may pass, but you should drive very carefully because the margin is extremely small.
You may not pass, as the law requires a safety margin of at least 20 centimeters.
You must lower the air suspension to its minimum setting before driving under the obstacle.
You must stop and measure the temperature of the road surface, as asphalt can expand in the heat.

questions.explanation: If it's summer, usually it should be okay to pass but the margin will be small. In winter time, the snow and ice on the pavement will make the margin smaller, so extra super careful as you proceed!

questions.question_text: You are driving a pickup truck that is registrated as a car which measures exactly 6.08 meters. Are you permitted to enter this road?

options.text: Yes; according to the rules, anything under 20 meters is permitted.
No. Vehicles or vehicle combinations exceeding the specified dimension are not permitted to pass
Yes, provided you activate your hazard lights and have an escort vehicle.
Yes, but only if you are driving without a trailer.

questions.explanation: This is a road sign for lorries, not for car drivers. In this area, it might be difficult to turn around or take turns, so large lorries are prohibited if they exceed 20 meters of length.

questions.question_text: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Gross weight of a vehicle must not exceed 12 000 kilograms past this sign
A vehicle on this road must have payed the toll for all vehicles weighing a gross weight of more than 12 tons
A vechicle is not allowed to be longer than 12 "thalns" which is an ancient swedish measurement
All vehicles may drive here but if your vehicle is heavier than 12 000 kilograms you have to have a special clearance for that

questions.explanation: 12 t means 12 000 kilograms. So the sign prohibits all traffic weighing more than that.

questions.question_text: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Gross weight of a vehicle combination must not exceed 30 000 kilograms past this sign
Total weight of a vehicle must not exceed 30 000 kilograms past this sign
Total weight of a vehicle combination must not exceed 30 000 kilograms past this sign
Cargo weight of a vehicle combination must not exceed 30 000 kilograms past this sign

questions.explanation: Gross weight is what the vehicle or vehicle combination weighs right here and right now. Total weight is the service weight plus cargo. Remember this!

questions.question_text: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Concerns lorries and buses and heavier vehicles, not a car driver. This is one of the road classes which determines how heavy a vehicle may be to drive on this road. BK3 is the weakest road, so I have to check how much every axel of my vehicle weighs in a special tabloid.
This means I am not allowed here, only lorries and buses are allowed to drive here.
This sign says a bridge is coming up and it's 3 tons maximum on the bridge, so I must be cautious not to have oncoming traffic while on the bridge!
This means environment zone 3, so hybrids and electric vehicles may drive here but nobody else

questions.explanation: BK 4 is the strongest roads, 74 000 kilograms is the max. Then BK 1 which makes up for about 90% of the swedish road network. BK 2 and BK 3 is a bit weaker roads and lorry drivers need to know their wight when driving here in order to know if it's allowed.

questions.question_text: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: This sign tells us that no axle on your vehicle is allowed to transfer more than 6 000 kilograms to the road at any given moment
It means no vehicle weighing more than 6000 kilograms may pass this sign
It says it's prohibited to go faster than 6 km/h
It prohibits rear-wheel driven cars over 6 tons

questions.explanation: A sign that we have to know what it means, but it doesn't affect us when we drive a car, since we are never that heavy. This sign is more relevant for lorry drivers. The number states the thousands of kilgrams allowed per axle.

questions.question_text: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: This sign tells us that no boggi/twin axle on your vehicle is allowed to transfer more than 10 000 kilograms to the road at any given moment
This sign tells us that no axle on your vehicle is allowed to transfer more than 12 000 kilograms to the road at any given moment
This is a prohibition for boggis longer than 12 meters
The sign says we must not drive here with 4x4 wheel drive due to the vibrations

questions.explanation: A sign that we have to know what it means, but it doesn't affect us when we drive a car, since we are never that heavy. This sign is more relevant for lorry drivers. the number states the thousands of kilgrams allowed per boggi /twin axle.

questions.question_text: What is the difference in Sweden between a light lorry and a heavy lorry?

options.text: A light lorry has a total weight of maximum 3500 kg
A heavy lorry is a lorry which can load weight over 750 kg
A lorry is a lorry, there was s no such thing as a light or a heavy lorry
That depends on the registration

questions.explanation: Total weight over 3500 kg is the rule. Repeat it.

questions.question_text: Some lorries have cargo that is especially dangerous. These types of cargo has to be marked internationally correct. How?

options.text: An orange sign that may or may not have numbers on it that tells which kind of cargo they carry indicates that the cargo is dangerous in some way
A diamond-shaped green sign means "dangerous goods - flammable" and is an international sign for dangerous goods
A diamond-shaped red sign means "dangerous goods" and is an international sign for dangerous goods
A diamond-shaped white sign means "dangerous goods" and is an international sign for dangerous goods

questions.explanation: There are several different characteristics which makes good dangerous. Flammable fluid, toxic, radioactive, explosive and others. All of them will have an orange sign, but also other signs which tells what kind of danger.

questions.question_text: What does this sign on a lorry in traffic mean?

options.text: It means the vehicle carries a significant amount of something dangerous in their goods
It means it's a heavy lorry with double axles
It means the lorry is a lorry and not a trailer, which can otherwise be hard to see from behind
It means this lorry carries living animals

questions.explanation: Why this is important to know is mainly if you arrive at the scene of a traffic accident and a lorry with this sign is involved. This means it's super dangerous, since it can be extra flammable, explosive, toxic, a super-flu that might spread, radioactive goo, or a combination.

questions.question_text: You are driving a fully loaded three-axle pickup truck with a high bogie load, and your drive axle exerts an actual load of 2000 kilograms on the road surface. What does this sign mean for you?

options.text: Nothing. I may proceed
You may not drive here since the vehicle's total weight exceeds 10 tonnes.
You may drive here if you lift the tag axle (non-driven axle) to redistribute the weight.
The sign applies only during the spring thaw; you are permitted to drive here during the rest of the year.

questions.explanation: It's a road sign for lorries, not for cars. You may proceed, you can be nowhere near this weight in a car anyway.

questions.question_text: What determines whether you are allowed to drive past this sign?

options.text: The actual weight (gross weight) of the vehicle or vehicle combination at that specific time must not exceed 12 tonnes.
It is the vehicle’s registered total weight—as stated on the registration document—that must never exceed 12 tonnes.
It is the weight of the load (the gross weight minus the maximum load capacity) that must not exceed 12 tonnes.
The prohibition applies only if the vehicle weighs less than 12 tonnes.

questions.explanation: It's a road sign for lorries, not for cars. You may proceed, you can be nowhere near this weight in a car anyway.

questions.question_text: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: This means I cannot pass this sign with any motor driven vehicle that has something towed behind, tow trucks not included in this
It means no lorries allowed
It means I am not allowed to park here or my car will be towed away
It means I can park here without having my car towed away

questions.explanation: No trailers, no caravans, no hay wagons behind the tractors, no nothing behind you! If however it's a weight limit attached to this road sign, there will be an additional sign and anything lighter is allowed.

questions.question_text: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: No lorries with a total weight over 3500 kilograms allowed
No lorries at all allowed
No lorries with a gross weight exceeding 7500 kilograms allowed
Your lorry can come but not if it's too high

questions.explanation: Light lorry with a total weight below 3500 kilograms counts as a regular car when we speak of most things traffic regulated.

questions.question_text: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: No tractors and also no motorized equipment vehicle class II allowed
No tractors class B allowed
No farmers
No tractors or lawnmowers allowed

questions.explanation: This goes for all tractors of any kind and all motorized equipment vehicles class II.

questions.question_text: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Probation for traffic with dangerous goods
Probation for lorries and trailers
Probation for all military vehicles
Probation for all vehicles with a total weight of more than 3500 kilograms

questions.explanation: Dangerous goods have special regulations and they are not allowed in certain tunnels and roads close to drinking water soucres and such.

questions.question_text: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: No bicycle traffic or moped class II traffic allowed (I can lead my bike next to me though)
Not even allowed to bring a bike leading it
No bicycle parking
All motorcycles, mopeds, bicycles strictly prohibited

questions.explanation: This sign can also be for moped class I, but then there will be an additional sign stating this.

questions.question_text: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: No traffic allowed with moped class I
No motorcycles or mopeds allowed
No two wheel vehicles allowed
No moped class I allowed, moped class II is allowed

questions.explanation: If this sign refers to Moped class I as well, an additional sign is added for this.

questions.question_text: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: No animal carriages allowed
No horses with a wagon allowed
No animals allowed
No farmers allowed

questions.explanation: Any animal that pulls a wagon is prohibited.

questions.question_text: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: No snowmobiles, no offroad trailers allowed
No snowmobiles allowed
It's impossible to drive a snowmobile here
No snowmobiles class I allowed here

questions.explanation: This sign is often found during the summer in nothern Sweden next to crop fields, sensitive parts of the mountains, planted forests and such, in order for the snowmobiles to not drive over the soil during winter.

questions.question_text: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: You are not allowed to ride your horse here but you may lead it
No more My Little Pony!
No horses allowed past this sign
Only horses under 300 kilograms rider included may sit in the saddle

questions.explanation: If this sign refers to leading your horse probation as well, an additional sign stating so will be added.

questions.question_text: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: No pedestrian traffic allowed past this sign
No males allowed
No humans allowed
No walking allowed but you may run or jog

questions.explanation: No one may walk here, run here, jog here or even step out of your vehicle after this sign. Usually put up at motorways and such.

questions.question_text: You are driving a small lorry of total weight 3440 kilograms, loaded with general cargo classified as dangerous goods (e.g., flammable liquids exceeding the calculated threshold quantity). What do you do when you see this sign?

options.text: You must choose a different route, as vehicles carrying dangerous goods are not permitted here
You may drive here if you switch off the truck’s main power disconnect while driving.
You may drive here if you have an approved fire extinguisher readily accessible in the cab.
The prohibition applies only in cities between 07:00 and 17:00.

questions.explanation: Most common close to sources of drinking water or tunnels.

questions.question_text: A yellow line crosses over the white broken line. Which one should you consider?

options.text: I follow the yellow line, since it's a temporary line and thus triumphs the regular white markings
I follow the white line since it is prohibited to drive in the onward-coming lane
I should never cross a white line no matter what
I should drive as if the lines are not there

questions.explanation: If they have painted a new line for the construction job, why would you not follow it? What would be the point of it being there, if not to tell us what to do? Always follow the temporary lines and signs.

questions.question_text: You are first on the scene of a traffic accident. A person is laying on the road, anxious and cold, sweating and out of breath. What is the most probable diagnos here?

options.text: Chock. Keep the person warm and check for injuries.
Probably a diabetic who needs insuline within the hour
Low blood flow to the feets, make them do 10-15 jumping jacks and then take deep, fast breaths
Possible kidneystone, perform a heimlish maneuever

questions.explanation: First, try to keep your calm. Panic will not help anyone. Assess the situation and get them away from danger if possible. Check their breathing. Check their body for blood leakage. Call for help. Warn others. Continue to help and assess the wounded. A broken arm is not lethal, a leaking artery is, so priority is important as well.

questions.question_text: What equipment is "nice to have" and what equipment is "need to have" of these?

options.text: Warning triangle is a must, it's required by law. Also it's nice to have a first aid kit just in case but you don't have to by law.
This is Sweden. A snow shovel is a must! A battery starter is nice to have.
A snow shovel is not a must, but a reflex west is. A warning triangle is nice to have but not needed according to the law.
A good knife in case I hit an animal and need to end it's suffering is a must, but some working gloves is nice to have.

questions.explanation: Warning triangle is required by the law to be in every car.

questions.question_text: In these situations, in which one is it correct to use your hazard lights?

options.text: In case that I have an engine failure and must stop at the side of the road, I may use hazard lights to warn others and make them understand the situation
If I have to stop at the side of the road to pick up a friend and it's not really a designated place for stopping
When I unload the vehicle on the airport
If I'm standing at a parking pocket along the highway in darkness, to make others know I'm there

questions.explanation: Hazard lights are for emergency only. If you must make yourself more visible but it's not an emergency, there are other lights for that. Parking light for example.

questions.question_text: What is a whiplash injury and in which part of the body is it likely that it occurs?

options.text: It's a neck injury usually originated from a collision
It's a knee injury, more common in mailmen who jump on and off their lorry many times a day
It's a spine injury that occurs in the lower back due to long days and sitting around a lot, usually occurs with taxi drivers
It's an old word that means sickness of the skin, your skin looks like it has been whipped

questions.explanation: Whiplash is something serious and painful. It doesn't show from the outside, but people might have to live with the consequences for the rest of their life with chronical pain in the neck after a collision.

questions.question_text: You see a police car behind you with blue blinking lights. What is the correct procedure for you?

options.text: I drive to the side of the road if possible to give the police a clear path
I stop at a safe place and await further instructions from the police, with my hands clearly visible on the steering wheel
I stop immediately and show them my driving licence
I await the police to overtake and guide me to a place to stop
