questions.explanation: In this case only blue lights, which means "Clear a path!" but if the light is red and blue it means "follow my instructions".

questions.question_text: You accidentally collide with a parked car at the parking lot. What is correct?

options.text: I risk losing my driving licence if I drive off from there.
I must call the Police
First I should contact my ensurance company to ask if I need to report it
If the other car was moving, I don't have to do anything

questions.explanation: Don't be a jerk! Leave a note with your phone number at the very least and take a picture för the insurance.

questions.question_text: What of the following alternatives is the best approach to a road construction site?

options.text: Lower your speed, follow the given instructions from temporary lines and temporary road signs, be a bit more alert
Give the construction vehicles extra space by driving closer to the car ahead
Follow the regular signs and lines as well as the temporary ones
It depends on if the road construction has personel outside of vehicles as I must only slow down if I see a risk

questions.question_text: If you are driving on a country road and another car makes a bad decision and overtakes you, and while doing so hit another oncoming vehicle, does the law say that you, who didn't collide, are obliged to stay on the scene?

options.text: Yes
No, since I was not part of the collision
Yes, but only if I wish to testify
No, but stop anyway and see if anyone is injured and if you may provide any help for them

questions.explanation: The law clearly states that any driver who was involved in any way must remain on the scene.

questions.question_text: Your engine dies unexpectedly on the country road during a drive in dark conditions. Which alternative is correct?

options.text: I stop on a safe place, as far to the side of the road as possible, turn on hazard lights, turn on light inside the car, open the trunk, put out a hazard triangle
I stop at the side of the road, turn on right blinkers and call a friend
I turn on high beam and fog lights, and call the police
I must remain in the car, but I can turn hazard lights on

questions.explanation: Hazard light and set up a triangle, these are a must. To put lights in the car on and pop the trunk makes you extra visible.

questions.question_text: You are at the scene of an accident on the road. Which one of these statements is correct?

options.text: Vehicles that has been part of the accident are only allowed to be moved if they create danger for others
Vehicles involved in the accident are only allowed to be moved by the police
Before moving a vehicle that has been in the accident, you must document the scene thoroughly with recording
You are allowed to move the vehicles 100 meters if you have the proper driving licence for that specific vehicle

questions.question_text: What is defensive driving, what does that mean?

options.text: Risk aware and ready to act on developments, cooperative with others, adapting to the situation to avoid traffic accidents
It means I will defend my position and not let others bully me. Follow the rules always, even if it becomes more dangerous
It means I always drive a little less than the speed limit
It means I put my seatbelt on and carry a first aid kit in my pocket, just in case.

questions.explanation: Defensive driving means to be aware of probable risks and to be proactive towards them. Most commonly by slowing down and be alert.

questions.question_text: What is significant for an experienced driver?

options.text: An experienced driver has more experience and will be better prepared for most traffic risks and has already taken measures for the risk before anything has even happened yet
An experienced driver can use smaller safety margins without increasing the risk of an accident
An experienced driver can talk on the phone while driving
Experienced drivers brakes more often than new drivers

questions.explanation: The reactions slows down with old age, but experience is such a big factor that most drivers that have been driving for years has built up a buffert that is compensating. Therefore, the driving style is more cautious and safe, so the risks never accur in the first place!

questions.question_text: Is there anything good at all about learning probabilities in traffic?

options.text: Yes, you should of course use your previous experience in order to avoid more common dangerous situations. You should however not calculate everything that you do based on what has happened before.
No, we must never assume anything in traffic.
No, we must first make sure that our experience has been approved by the Transport agency
Yes, we can always assume that the probable scenario will transpire

questions.explanation: Experience is good. Stupidity is not. Use your common sense! Murphy's law stipulates that anything that can happen sooner or later will happen. This is definitely true regarding traffic. Expect the expected, but be prepared for the unexpected as well.

questions.question_text: Should you seek eye contact with a bicyclist who tries to cross the street at a pedestrian crosswalk zebra?

options.text: Yes. Eye contact is good to avoid misunderstandings
No, I should not lure them away from their focus, they need to check their blind spot, not look at me.
No, since I do not wish to give them false sense of safety
Only if they are smiling

questions.explanation: This might be difficult in darkness, but generally it's a good thing. You should however never ever wave them to go, because that is their responsibility, not yours.

questions.question_text: Most traffic accidents happens because of the human factor. How should we behave as drivers to drive safer?

options.text: We should adapt our speed and placement to our current situation and be risk-aware, try to drive as predictable as possible
We should always follow the rules
We should avoid dangerous car models
We should drive extra slow on the entrance ramp onto the highway so we have time to react

questions.explanation: A predictable driver that drives as expected is easier for others to adapt to. Order creates safety.

questions.question_text: Should blinkers be used to tell others when I leave the side of the road and drive onto the road again?

options.text: Yes
No
Only if others are in my proximity
It's not against the law, I can choose to do so to be nice
